articles.title: School protests send shivers down French government's spine
articles.summary: A movement that started nearly two weeks ago has spread, and in France young people on the streets spells trouble, writes Hugh Schofield.

blocks.text: It is a piece of wisdom that all French leaders take care to heed: young people on the street equals trouble.
Since the student protests of May 1968 – memorably described by President De Gaulle as chienlit (bed defecation, in other words chaos) – every government has run scared of angry French youth.
Why? Because youth movements are unpredictable and shapeless, often with no clear structure to negotiate with. Because when they protest, other groups join in.

Also: because as they're young, the public tends to sympathise. And because if the police mess up and cause injury or worse, then the consequences are incalculable. And presidential elections are only months away.
For all these reasons, when la jeunesse en colère (angry youth) is at the barricades governments tread very carefully indeed.

Right now, French teenagers are at the barricades and if they are not visibly angry (the mood is more excitement), they certainly have the government of President Emmanuel Macron in what Le Monde called on Friday "the cold sweats".
A movement that started nearly two weeks ago in the low-income Seine-Saint-Denis area of northern Paris has in the last few days spread across the country.

An internal report prepared for the Paris police department which was leaked to the media analysed the opening of the movement in Seine-Saint-Denis. It concluded that students were being "egged on by far-left elements from students unions… and political groups such as… LFI."
It said the tensions "could be part of a flame-kindling strategy… aimed at imposing their ideas ahead of the national elections".

In support of its conclusion, the report's writers cited the presence of protesters who are not themselves lycéens, the vagueness of the demands, the flying of Palestinian and Algerian flags, and the use of tactics – like calling for supplementary protests at police-stations - that come from the radical-left playbook.

The LFI strongly denies doing anything more than lending its natural support to a movement it regards as legitimate. On Thursday Mélenchon called on students to avoid violence "which only serves our enemies' interests".

But his opponents believe that the 75-year-old veteran – who stands a good chance of making it to the second round of the presidential elections in May, probably against the hard-right's Marine Le Pen – knows exactly what he is doing.

Polls show he has massive support – some 40% -- among 18-24 year-olds in France, and that this is concentrated in the populous, high-immigration city suburbs where his talk of a "new France" and "creolisation", to reflect France's changing language and population, are highly appreciated.

But young people are also the biggest abstainers in French elections, so the strategy – as the elections approach – will be to give constant reminders to this part of the population that the LFI is at their side, and that their vote can count.
Whether this will be enough to ensure victory for Mélenchon is another matter. He must surely take seriously the polls which all show him losing massively in a run-off against Le Pen.
If that happens, France will be in very unstable territory - for which the young people's protests of recent days will indeed have been a harbinger.

articles.title: Napolis provides silver lining with jiu-jitsu bronze after Ramirez, Custodio heartbreaks in Asian Games
articles.summary: Kaila Napolis breaks through for the Philippine jiu-jitsu team in the 2026 Asian Games with a bronze medal after world champions Annie Ramirez and Kimberly Custodio suffered surprise early exits

blocks.text: WIN. Jiu-jitsu athlete Kaila Napolis in action for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
Kaila Napolis breaks through for the Philippine jiu-jitsu team in the 2026 Asian Games with a bronze medal after world champions Annie Ramirez and Kimberly Custodio suffered surprise early exits

items: Kaila Napolis won a bronze medal in jiu-jitsu at the 2026 Asian Games, marking the Philippines' only jiu-jitsu medal in the event.
Napolis secured her medal after defeating Mongolia's Tsagaanbileg Altangerel 2-0, following a loss in the quarterfinals.
Her victory came after the disappointing exits of fellow competitors Annie Ramirez and Kimberly Custodio, who were expected to perform well.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Kaila Napolis somehow made up for the heartbreaking defeats of world champions Annie Ramirez and Kimberly Custodio as she salvaged a jiu-jitsu bronze medal in the 2026 Asian Games.

Napolis clinched what is so far the Philippines’ only jiu-jitsu medal in the continental meet in Nagoya, Japan, after a 2-0 win over Mongolia’s Tsagaanbileg Altangerel in the battle for the women’s 52kg bronze at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall on Friday, October 2.

A Southeast Asian Games champion, Napolis crashed out of gold-medal contention after a 3-2 loss to to Mongolia’s Mongoljin Ganbaatar in the quarterfinals, but she found her way to the podium by coming out triumphant in the repechage against Singapore’s Sofia Anabel Rivas and toppling Altangerel for the bronze.
“I really wanted to bounce back [and end] with the bronze medal. I wanna give it all. And thankfully, I pulled it off,” said Napolis in a mix of Filipino and English.
Napolis replicated her campaign in the 2023 edition in Hangzhou, China, where she also won bronze after losing in the semifinals.

Her podium finish came after the surprise exits of Ramirez and Custodio, who were tipped as strong gold-medal contenders following their triumphs in the Ju-Jitsu International Federation World Championships in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, in August.

Eyeing a second Asian Games gold after ruling the women’s 57kg class in 2023, Ramirez lost her opening match as she competed in the lighter 52kg division, falling to Thailand’s Nuchanat Singchalad in the round of 16 on Friday.
The match ended in a scoreless tie, but Singchalad advanced by virtue of her two advantage points.

Meanwhile, Custodio — a four-time world champion in the women’s 45kg category — saw action in the heavier 48kg class, where she exited the round of 16 against UAE’s Balqees Abdulla on Thursday, October 1.
Similar to the fate Ramirez suffered, Custodio lost via advantage.
“We’re a bit sad, of course, for those who did not medal. But I’m still super thankful for the support,” said Napolis. – Rappler.com

articles.title: VP Sara Duterte, Mans Carpio accepted money from China --Trillanes
articles.summary: Former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV accused Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, lawyer Maneses Carpio, of respectively accepting P150 million and P319 million through their separate…

blocks.text: Published October 2, 2026 8:19pm

Former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV accused Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, lawyer Maneses Carpio, of respectively accepting P150 million and P319 million through their separate organizations.
In a "24 Oras" report from Sandra Aguinaldo on Friday, Trillanes presented the evidence he was supposed to show the impeachment court before the prosecution removed him as a witness.
“Tumanggap sila ng P150 million from the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China, itong foundation ni Sara Duterte,” Trillanes said.
(Sara Duterte’s foundation accepted P150 million from the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China.)
Trillanes also alleged that Carpio received P319 million from the Chinese government through his company.

“Ito na ang paraan ng China ng pagsuporta sa mag-asawang Duterte, maliwanag po ito. Kaya dapat kikilabutan po tayo rito, kasi vice president po siya, may national security implications, bawal po yan,” Trillanes said.
(This is how China is supporting the Duterte couple; it is clear. So we should be afraid, because she is the vice president; there is a national security concern, this is not allowed.)
GMA News has sought the reaction of the Vice President's camp and will update the story once it is available.
Duterte also allegedly failed to declare in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth her peso and dollar time deposit and insurance, the former lawmaker said.

Trillanes said that he himself initiated his removal as a witness in Duterte’s impeachment trial to remove pressure from the prosecution panel, however, he did not disclose further details about this.
“Sa akin naman kasi the signal is clear. Hindi ako welcome,” Trillanes said. (For me, the signal is clear. I am not welcome.)
He also criticized impeachment presiding officer Chiz Escudero for his handling of the proceedings, saying that he should be more liberal.
“Bantayan niyo yung presiding officer. That's what I'm saying. Tignan nyo,” Trillanes said. (Guard the presiding officer. That's what I'm saying. Look at him.)
Impeachment court spokesperson Regie Tongol dismissed the claim that Trillanes was not welcome, as he was treated like a guest when he attended the trial. —LDF, GMA News

items: The Philippines missed out on two gold medals in taekwondo at the 2026 Asian Games, with Tachiana Mangin and Kurt Barbosa winning silver instead.
Mangin lost to China's Ma Jingyue in the women's -49kg final, while Barbosa was defeated by Kazakhstan's Tamirlan Tleules in the men's -58kg final.
Despite the losses, both athletes had strong performances, with Mangin making her Asian Games debut and Barbosa improving from his previous competition results.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines missed out on two additional gold medals in the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, after taekwondo jins Tachiana Mangin and Kurt Barbosa settled for a pair of silvers on Friday, October 2.

Barbosa and Mangin lost their respective title bouts at the Toyohashi Gymnasium as they fell short of delivering another gold in the sport after Jeus Gabriel Derick Yape ruled in the mixed individual virtual taekwondo earlier in the day.
Mangin saw her superb run come to a disappointing end at the hands of China’s Ma Jingyue, who pulled off a 2-0 victory in the women’s -49kg finale.
The two rounds each ended in a scoreless tie, but the Chinese won both by superiority to claim the gold medal.
Still, it was a promising campaign for Mangin as she won a medal on her Asian Games debut at just 18 years old.

A former world junior champion and a Southeast Asian Games titlist, Mangin beat Kazakhstan’s Rita Bakisheva in the round of 16, Chinese Taipei’s Wang Chieh-ling in the quarterfinals, and Japan’s Ruka Okamoto in the semifinals to get a crack at the crown.
Meanwhile, Barbosa absorbed a 16-14, 15-2 loss to Kazakhstan’s Tamirlan Tleules in the men’s -58kg final.
After losing a nip-and-tuck opening frame, Barbosa sought to pull level in the second round, but Tleules landed two straight head kicks to seal his golden victory.

Despite the defeat, the pride of Abra redeemed himself from his campaign in the 2023 edition in Hangzhou, China, where he lost his opening match in the round of 32. The Tokyo Olympian also bounced back from his failed four-peat bid in the 2025 Southeast Asian Games in Bangkok, Thailand.

Barbosa reached the final by stunning Asian champion Jafar Aldaoud of Jordan in the semifinals, following up on his victories over Saudi Arabia’s Abdullah Essa Almushraf in the round of 16 and Japan’s Hidetaka Maeda in the quarterfinals.
A win by either Mangin and Barbosa would have marked the first time the Philippines won at least five golds in an Asian Games edition since its seven-gold haul in 1962.
The country currently has four golds courtesy of Yape, gymnastics star Carlos Yulo (with two golds), and pole vault ace EJ Obiena. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Manchester City Premier League charges: What do they mean?
articles.summary: Since being bought by the UAE in 2008, Manchester City have become one of the world's most successful football clubs. A raft of serious financial charges threatens to undermine this and bring chaos…

image.caption: Sheikh Mansour, as he is widely known, fronted the deal to buy City for the UAE nearly 20 years agoImage: Martin Rickett/PA Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: Manchester City has won the English Premier League eight times over the last 14 years. Whether those titles will remain is one of a plethora of issues at stake after England's top division charged one of its most high-profile clubs with more than 100 breaches of its financial regulations.

On Tuesday, the Premier League announced that an independent commission had found City had drawn up "sham contracts" as well as "relying on sham agreements to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs." These contracts, dubious sponsorships and a number of other methods were, according to the commission's report, used to inflate the club's revenue to the tune of about £900 million (€1.05 billion) over the period between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.
The case has been ongoing for eight years after initial revelations from Der Spiegel, a German magazine, and Rui Pinto of the 'Football Leaks' website. City continues to deny any wrongdoing.

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case," read a club statement. "Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."
On Friday, the club issued a further statement saying it had lodged a "comprehensive Appeal."
What was the Premier League verdict on the Manchester City charges?

The 750-page report was damning, accusing City of inflating contracts and sponsorship deals, running secondary contracts off the books, making "concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the Premier League investigation" and signing off inflated image rights deals to artificially boost their earnings. The report says all this enabled them to pass both Premier League and UEFA financial spending limits.

The Premier League's chief ­executive, Richard Masters, described the case "as the most significant in Premier League history," adding that the club "systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade."

Although the Premier League, the world's most commercially successful football league, has drawn some praise for its actions, others point out that it took Pinto leaking emails and media reports to take action. The report shows that Manchester City, which had won the league once in 71 years before being taken over by the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in 2008, were consistently posting revenues way higher than any of their more established and successful rivals.
Who are the key figures at Manchester City?

In this context, its the owners. The Abu Dhabi United Group, essentially an investment vehicle for the UAE royal family, bought the club in 2008. Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, know simply as Sheikh Mansour, fronted the takeover. He is a member of the ruling Al Nahyan family and the UAE's vice president and deputy prime minister. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, who also holds several government positions in the UAE, was brought in as chairman.

Nation-state ownership of this type is controversial in European football. Manchester City's owners have long been criticized for the country's human rights record and using the club for sportswashing. Similar criticisms have been made of European champions Paris Saint-Germain, which Qatar owned and City's Premier League rivals Newcastle United, which is owned 85% by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund.

blocks.caption: As well as huge domestic success, City won the Champions League under Pep Guardiola in 2022-23Image: Jose Breton/NurPhoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: City's CEO, Ferran Soriano, joined in 2012 as City expanded their ownership into foreign leagues, buying up clubs in the US, Japan and Australia. He replaced former head coach Roberto Mancini with fellow Spaniard Manuel Pellegrini before former Bayern Munich and Barcelona coach Pep Guardiola took over in 2016, ushering in the club's most successful period.
How did Manchester City's system work?

The club immediately started splashing out on big-money transfers after the UAE investment arrived. At the time, neither UEFA nor the Premier League had the tight financial rules they now have. UEFA introduced its Financial Fair Play (FFP) rules for the 2011-12 season, while the Premier League followed with its Profit and Sustainability Rules (PSR) in 2013-14.

City's free spending and relatively low commercial income meant they were likely to fall foul of such rules. The club was handed a conditional €60 million UEFA fine for losses in the 2011-12 and 2012-13 seasons. They would later be banned from the Champions League on similar grounds in 2020 before being reinstated on appeal.

In an attempt to try and comply with these financial rules, City set up a system they called "Project Longbow" in 2012. The commission said much of this was genuine, but one arm of it was an agreement with a third party called Fordham that was, according to the ruling, "little more than a front." Essentially, it reads, the club's UAE owners "would be used (and were used) to enable Fordham to acquire from the club (at a sizeable, artificially inflated price) the club's entitlement to benefit financially from its players' image rights."

In other words, City's owners were pumping money into their own club through vastly inflated sponsorship and image rights deals so their income looked higher and they could spend more, particularly on player transfers and wages. The report also claims that City paid three individuals, whose names are redacted, through a third party to keep them off the books.
What happens next?

That's the question on everyone's lips. So far, no sanctions have been imposed on City, and the appeal will likely drag proceedings out even longer. Meanwhile, the club, which is top of the Premier League, faces Liverpool on October 11, after the international break.

While there is no precedent for such a tranche of charges, clubs have previously fallen foul of the Premier League's PSR regulations. Everton were handed a 10-point penalty for a £19.5 million breach over a period ending with the 2021-22 season. This was based on a Premier League tariff of six points for the initial breach, plus an additional point for every £5 million the club overspent. Given that City's overspending is close to a billion pounds, applying that would certainly relegate them, though the Premier League does not operate England's second-tier league, the Championship.

For now, it looks like City and the league will play on under a cloud. But if the verdict remains after appeal, clubs and individuals whose careers and honors stand to be impacted will likely come forward and litigate. City themselves could be relegated, docked points over successive seasons, face transfer bans or any combination of those things. The titles won in the relevant period could also be stripped.
This article was originally published on September 30, 2026. It was updated on October 2, 20206 with Manchester City's statement confirming that it had lodged an appeal.

articles.title: Fictitious name? The curious case of ‘Ang Hai Peng,’ Sara Duterte’s biz partner
articles.summary: Ask former senator Antonio Trillanes IV, and he will tell you it's a person who doesn't exist.

blocks.text: Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV alleges on October 2, 2026 that the name Ang Hai Peng in the corporate records of a company tied to Vice President Sara Duterte belongs to a person who does not exist.
Rappler screenshot
Ask former senator Antonio Trillanes IV, and he will tell you it's a person who doesn't exist.
Who is behind the Chinese name that had appeared — but later disappeared — in the corporate records of Vice President Sara Duterte’s company?
Ask former senator Antonio Trillanes IV, and he will tell you it’s a person who doesn’t exist.

During his press conference on Friday, October 2, Trillanes put the spotlight on Ang Hai Peng, which Trillanes said appeared in the records of Timesquare Bee Foods, a company incorporated by Duterte, as per her assets list over the years.
Trillanes said the company’s corporate documents showed that Ang owned 60% of the company from 2013 to 2013. The company was later renamed Gencorp.
Gencorp’s records with the Securities and Exchange Commission didn’t bear Ang’s name beginning 2022. The top shareholder has become the JTC Group of Companies, owned by Jaime T. Cruz.
Cruz is a business partner of the Dutertes. His name appears in numerous corporate documents co-owned by the Vice President, her husband Mans Carpio, and her siblings Paolo and Sebastian Duterte.
Central to Trillanes’ allegation is that Peng does not have government records.
“They have no birth certificate, they have no passport, their TIN is fake, and, incidentally, their birthday is the same as Jaime T. Cruz’s,” Trillanes claimed.
“They are one person. I am one hundred percent person that [Ang Hai Peng] is nonexistent,” he added.

blocks.caption: Fictitious name? The curious case of ‘Ang Hai Peng,’ Sara Duterte’s biz partner

blocks.text: We have emailed JTC Group of Companies’ email address for Cruz’s side of the story. We will update this story once we receive a reply.

Rappler first reported about Jaime T. Cruz in mid-September as part of our exposé on Gencorp and how it has bagged millions of pesos in contracts with Davao City Hall led by Mayor Sebastian since 2022. The arrangement raises conflict of interest and constitutional violation issues against the Vice President.
The prosecution’s team has zeroed in on Gencorp at the impeachment court, but it has yet to say whether it will actually call Cruz a witness.
With Trillanes no longer in prosecution’s witness lineup, it remains to be seen whether the issue he has raised will find their way somehow into the impeachment court. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Half of Europe witnessed record heat stress this summer — EU
articles.summary: The EU's climate monitor said this summer was third-warmest for the continent on record. European rivers also registered their lowest average flows since records began in 1992.

image.caption: Europeans across the continent had to cool themselves off during repeated heat waves [FILE: July 30, 2026]Image: Volodymyr Sindieiev/picture alliance

blocks.text: A record 52% of Europe witnessed "very strong" heat stress by the end of this summer, the EU's Copernicus Climate Service (C3S) said in new research published on Friday.
What did Copernicus say in its findings?
According to Copernicus, "very strong" heat stress is characterized by temperatures which feel higher than 38 degrees Celsius (100.4 degrees Fahrenheit).
Around 80% of Europe witnessed "strong" heat stress by the end of the summer. "Strong" heat stress is when temperatures feel like more than 32 degrees Celsius (89.6 degrees Fahrenheit).
Heat stress is when temperatures and humidity are so high that the body cannot cool itself through perspiration.
This summer was the third-warmest on record on the European continent and the hottest on record in Western Europe.
"One of the things that stands out for 2026 is that the heat was not only remarkable for its intensity, but also for its geographical extent," Samantha Burgess, the deputy director of the C3S, said.

blocks.caption: The Rhine River in western Germany saw record lows during the heat waves this summer Image: Hesham Elsherif/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: Copernicus also said that European rivers registered their lowest average flows since records began in 1992. In addition, the service said that "56% of the European ocean was much warmer than average, with 22% experiencing record-high summer sea surface temperatures."
Burgess said that drought impacted almost half of Europe by the end of this summer.
"That's one of the defining characteristics of summer this year, that it was not a single record. It was the way that multiple records appeared together across the climate system," she said.
What was the impact of the European heat waves this summer?
Tens of thousands of people died in heat waves in Europe this summer, which also impacted economic activity and agricultural harvests.
Some cities such as Paris even temporarily restricted alcohol sales as temperatures frequently spiked above 40 degrees Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit) on parts of the continent.
Air conditioning is uncommon in some parts of Europe, with many Europeans staying home or going out to the pool to cool off.
France's firefighters on the wildfire frontline
In addition, the frequent heat waves and dry conditions this summer also led to wildfires in southern France and the southern Spanish region of Andalusia, among other locations.
The biggest wildfire in history in Germany's most populous state, North Rhine-Westphalia, triggered evacuations in August before it was brought under control.
Wildfires not only damage buildings but also create harmful air pollution in the environment.

articles.title: P5B budget sought for sugar industry, restricted importation in new bill
articles.summary: A bill seeking a P5 billion budget for the sugar industry and restrictions on sugar importation was filed in the House of Representatives.

blocks.text: Published October 2, 2026 7:49pm
A bill seeking a P5 billion budget for the sugar industry and restrictions on sugar importation was filed in the House of Representatives.

Negros Occidental 3rd District Rep. Javier Miguel “Javi” Benitez made the proposal under House Bill 9088, or Tunay na Ugnayan, Buhay, at Oportunidad sa Asukal (TUBO) Act, a measure which he announced during a LegisHear public consultation in Victorias City in his home province.

Benitez said the measure seeks to address problems exposed by previous sugar importation, strengthen support for farmers, and make government decisions affecting the industry more transparent and firmly anchored on production, inventory, and consumption data.

Benitez said the measure provides that, of the said P5 billion annual budget starting 2027, 30 percent will go to farm-to-mill roads and irrigation while 20 percent will be earmarked for climate adaptation and resilience.
“The bill fixes where it goes, so nobody can quietly move it,” Benitez said.

“This increased funding has become more urgent because of the spread of the red-striped soft scale insect (RSSI), which, as of September 1, had affected 134,000 hectares nationwide, including 95,000 hectares in Negros Occidental,” he added.
Likewise, Benitez said the measure provides for an 18-month pause on commercial sugar imports upon effectivity, subject to an exception for verified shortages.
After the said pause, imports would be permitted only when warranted by supply data and would be prohibited during the first three months of the milling season.
Further, the measure sets a trigger allowing imports when verified raw sugar stocks fall below 200,000 tons.
This way, Benitez said importation will only be merit-based instead of a whimsical decision.
“[Because] when an import decision is made by order, without data and without the people who grow the cane, the farmer carries the cost,” Benitez said.
Benitez’s proposal would also require random and unannounced audits of mill laboratories, with penalties including fines, suspension or loss of license for tampering.

In addition, the bill requires sugar orders to be published within 15 days together with votes and dissents, establish a public dashboard tracking the use and beneficiaries of industry funds, and provide for twice-yearly consultations with farmers, workers, agrarian reform beneficiaries, millers and refiners.

Other assistance provided in the measure includes block farming, socialized credit, discounts of up to 30 percent on fertilizer and machinery, emergency cash assistance during pest outbreaks or calamities, temporary relief from loan penalties, price-support purchases, auditable mill measurements, and farm-to-mill infrastructure.
Benitez, however, said the bill is still subject to the feedback of sugar farmers and other stakeholders.

“This bill remains under consideration, and the inputs gathered from sugar farmers and other stakeholders during LegisHear would feed into the work of the technical working group,” he said. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: This island in Kiribati could be the key to solve the Amelia Earhart mystery
articles.summary: Nearly 90 years after US aviator Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific, a new expedition to the remote island of Nikumaroro hopes a lagoon anomaly could finally reveal the fate of her missing…

image.caption: Amelia Earhart disappeared in the South Pacific in 1937 while on an around-the-world flightImage: picture alliance / Courtesy Everett Collection

blocks.text: Amelia Earhart's attempt to become the first woman to fly around the globe at the equator ended in mystery when she and her navigator, Fred Noonan, disappeared over the Pacific Ocean in July 1937.

With the 90th anniversary of her disappearance on the horizon, a new expedition is setting out to finally determine what happened over the vast Pacific. This expedition has what it believes is crucial new evidence.

The team from Purdue University in Indiana and the Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) is scheduled to depart for the uninhabited island of Nikumaroro on Saturday to determine if an anomaly in the island's lagoon is Earhart's missing plane.
Part of the low-lying Pacific island nation of Kiribati, Nikumaroro has long been considered the place where Earhart and Noonan died.
The pair took off from New Guinea on July 2, 1937, on the leg to the island of Howland, where they were to refuel before continuing on to Hawaii and completing the circumnavigation in California.

blocks.caption: Amelia Earhart, left, and navigator Fred Noonan hold a map of the Pacific Ocean showing the planned route of their flightImage: picture alliance / AP Photo

blocks.text: Something went amiss en route, however, and even though a US Coast Guard ship could hear Earhart's radio transmissions and her Lockheed Electra must have been tantalizingly close, she was never found.
One of the last messages said she was running on a north-south navigational line that gave her the best chance of finding land before her fuel ran out. That line went through Nikumaroro.
Landing on a coral reef
In 1988, researchers from the International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery (TIGHAR) were the first to suggest that Earhart could have reached Nikumaroro and landed on its fringing coral reef.
TIGHAR's first visit to the island was in 1989, and the group has returned seven more times, turning up compelling artifacts, including lengths of aircraft aluminum and plexiglass from a windscreen.
The group found a scent bottle, a zip made in Pennsylvania in the mid-1930s, parts of a pocket knife of the same brand listed in the aircraft inventory, and the heel of a woman's shoe.
Archive research discovered that human remains discovered on the island in 1940 were initially believed to be of Earhart or Noonan — but were lost in the chaos of the Pacific war.
Despite the searches, no one has yet found the "smoking gun" artifact, an item that could only have come from the doomed flight.
Satellite images offer fresh hope
Expedition leader Rick Pettigrew, executive director of the Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI), believes the elements may have uncovered incontrovertible evidence.

A powerful tropical cyclone tore through the central Pacific in 2015, shifting geographical features on the island and in its lagoon. Satellite images taken over the following years showed what might be the outline of an aircraft fuselage and wings in shallow water off the Taraia promontory.

"This object in the satellite images is exactly the right size to represent the fuselage and tail of the Electra," the ALI website states. "It also appears to be very reflective and is likely to be metallic. It lies in very shallow water, largely covered by sediment, in a place where the current would bring an object floating into the lagoon through Tatiman Passage, the opening to the ocean and the reef."

Pettigrew's 17-strong team intends to focus all its efforts on the place where the images indicate debris may be located, using drone photography, remote sensing with magnetometers and sonar units. If the initial results are positive, a hydraulic dredge will excavate sediment.

"Once we have a sufficient portion of the object exposed, we should be able to identify it," according to the ALI's expedition plan. "If it is made of aircraft aluminum and has the specific shape and rivet patterns of the Electra, we will know that we have found the remains of Earhart's aircraft."
In search of a 'smoking gun'
Much of the ALI's theory is based on the research and fieldwork carried out by TIGHAR, but its executive director, Ric Gillespie, is not convinced the researchers will find the "smoking gun."

blocks.caption: The expedition to Nikumaroro could finally resolve a mystery that has endured for nearly 90 yearsImage: Google Earth

blocks.text: "The object visible in old satellite imagery that Pettigrew believes is aircraft wreckage does not look like aircraft wreckage," Gillespie told DW. "It looks like a dead pandanus tree that was uprooted in a storm and washed up on Taraia."

"Pettigrew thinks the wreckage is no longer visible because it is buried in silt," Gillespie noted. "He has never been to that location and does not understand that the silt there is only a few inches deep."
Teams from TIGHAR searched the same location in 2001 and 2007 with metal detectors and drew blanks, he said. Yet Gillespie remains convinced that Earhart was on Nikumaroro.

"I think the aircraft sank immediately after being washed over the reef edge and was smashed to pieces in the surf," he said. "Major components were eventually buried in underwater landslides … or grown over with coral. We have found what there is to find."

Dorothy Cochrane, who has monitored progress in the search for Earhart for more than 35 years as curator at the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Washington, DC, and continues to do so since her recent retirement, says Earhart still holds fascination for so many people "because it is 'the greatest unsolved mystery of the 20th and continuing into the 21st centuries.'"
An alternative scenario

She has a different view of what happened in 1937. She argues that if Earhart was nearly out of fuel while still close to Howland, it would have been impossible to fly another 640 kilometers (400 miles) to Nikumaroro. Cochrane also says that items cited as evidence of a castaway on the island can be explained by other visitors and by a small settlement that existed there for several years.
"I believe that Earhart and Noonan were in the general vicinity of Howland Island, based on the facts of the flight, but just could not find it before they ran out of fuel," she said.
"Howland Island was a tiny speck in the morning light of a vast sea," she said, suggesting Earhart could not establish radio contact to guide her the last few miles to her destination.
Cochrane believes the Electra lies on the seabed near Howland. Others have advanced this theory, and several searches of the area have been carried out in recent years.
If Pettigrew's lead pays off, however, it will conclude aviation's nearly 90-year puzzle.

articles.title: Government inspection at 3 Ontario career colleges reported 'serious concerns,' court records show
articles.summary: Ontario government officials who inspected three Academy of Learning career colleges found evidence suggesting third parties were completing the coursework and a few students who couldn't name their…

image.caption: Colleges and Universities Minister Nolan Quinn informed five career colleges earlier this year that they would not be OSAP eligible, after they failed an inspection last year. (Diona Macalinga/CBC)

blocks.text: Ontario government officials who inspected three career colleges found evidence suggesting third parties were completing the coursework — sometimes entire courses in one day — and a few students who couldn't name their school or program, they alleged in reports filed in court.

Inspection reports for three Academy of Learning locations are among hundreds of pages of documents that make up the record in a court challenge as the schools seek to overturn a government decision that cut off their ability to offer financial aid.

"Inspection findings indicate that AOL Bay is unable to demonstrate that OSAP-funded students are actively participating in the programs they are enrolled in," the government's OSAP compliance unit wrote in a September 2025 inspection report for a downtown Toronto location.
"This raises serious concerns about the reliability of the institution’s admissions practices, student identity verification, and the accuracy of academic progression and attendance records."
The schools deny most of the allegations and also say they have taken the government's concerns seriously, including already implementing numerous corrective actions.

The three Academy of Learning locations are among 10 that Career Colleges Ontario flagged for the government in January 2025 as having "concerning" levels of growth in applications for the Ontario Student Assistance Program — jumping 500 and 600 per cent in two years — while other schools' activity was largely flat, the college association said in a letter.
OSAP changes are in effect. Here’s how students are being impacted

Data obtained by The Canadian Press through a freedom-of-information request found that about 14,800 students at those three Academy of Learning franchise locations received more than $219 million in OSAP grants in 2024-25.
Meanwhile, students at all publicly funded colleges across Ontario qualified for about $385 million in OSAP grants that year, freedom-of-information data shows.

Colleges and Universities Minister Nolan Quinn informed five career colleges, including the three Academy of Learning locations, on May 1 that they would not be OSAP eligible as of Aug. 1. The three schools, which share a parent company, have applied for judicial review of that decision, alleging Quinn did not have the power to predetermine their eligibility for this year and that his decision is unreasonable.
Ineligible schools failed inspection, court records show

Court records show Quinn's decision followed inspections last year and earlier this year that inspectors say the schools failed, with the ministry listing similar concerns in both reports. One report covers two sites, as a North York location is a branch campus of Academy of Learning Brampton East.

One student's account showed all of their quizzes and final exam in their business writing essentials course were completed on the same day, with the final exam taking six minutes, the Brampton inspection report said.

Another Brampton student's account shows their final exam for a business course was completed on the first day they accessed the course, inspectors wrote. Yet another student viewed all of their business writing essentials modules and completed all quizzes on the same day in less than 15 minutes, inspectors wrote.
The credentials of a student at the North York campus were used to log into their school account from at least 211 IP addresses, inspectors wrote.

At the Bay Street location, 39 out of 42 student files examined by inspectors had IP addresses that were used to access accounts belonging to other students, who were all referred by the same recruiter, the report said.
How much OSAP are students getting this school year?
"This pattern suggests shared login credentials, unauthorized access, and/or co-ordinated activity among users," the report said.

"While shared networks or communal access points, such as residences or campus locations, could explain IP address overlap, the frequency and concentration of these shared IP addresses within specific community partners is notable."
The nature of the inspectors' findings prompted them to drill down further and contact six students, three of whom were available for a phone call.

Interviews revealed "inconsistencies," including students unable to name their institution, program or courses, students unable to communicate in English and students claiming to attend classes in person despite being enrolled in asynchronous online programs, the inspectors wrote.
The federal government also expressed concerns about the Bay and Brampton locations in September 2025, according to letters sent to the institutions that are also part of the court record.

items: OSAP delay sends Ontario college students home on 1st day of school
Students at 7 Ontario private career colleges received $385M in OSAP grants last year, data shows

blocks.text: The government alleged unusually high growth in the amount of financial aid claimants from the schools, that there was evidence that multiple applications were completed by the same person or group, significant increases in loan default rates and that a large amount of people could not be confirmed as qualifying students.

In a February 2026 letter to the province, also in the court record, Career Colleges Ontario said the federal government's concerns and subsequent investigations led to reduced OSAP application volumes at those schools, but "application activity shifted to other institutions rather than declining."

"This pattern aligns with complaints received from CCO members indicating that certain schools were using third-party agents who offered to redirect students to other institutions if those institutions would misrepresent or falsely report attendance in order to facilitate continued OSAP disbursement," executive director Kate Bartz wrote.
None of the findings and allegations from either level of government have been proven in court.
Academy denies government allegations
The Academy of Learning denies most of the allegations from both levels of government and the ways in which some of their evidence is being interpreted.

Students may not have responded to the federal government's verification attempts because they believed them to be scam calls, and other students having difficulty answering questions in interviews "can be reasonably attributed to situational and linguistic factors," the school wrote in response to the government.

The Academy of Learning also offered up, in its response, figures showing their loan default rates to not be high, and it suggested the high growth in applications was due to offering programs relevant to workforce needs.
The schools also wrote to the province to rebut any nefarious assumptions about students' log-ins from multiple IP address, saying Bell, Rogers and Cogeco customers are assigned dynamic IP addresses.
"The presence of the same IP address among different users does not, by itself, establish misconduct, misrepresentation, or unauthorized activity," they wrote.
Why Ontario students staged a mass protest over Ford's OSAP cuts
As well, the schools had submitted corrective action plans in response to their failed inspections, showing dozens of actions taken to remedy problems identified by the province.

The Academy of Learning said in a statement that many of the government concerns relate to a historical period that has since been the subject of "extensive regulatory review, corrective action plans, internal reviews, and independent compliance monitoring."

"Since these concerns were raised, we have put in place significant additional controls across admissions, identity verification, financial aid, and academic participation and progress," the school wrote in a statement.

"These include two-factor authentication and investigation of unusual login activity. We have co-operated extensively with both reviews and will continue to strengthen our controls wherever issues are identified."

items: 'Suspicious' OSAP activity at some career colleges flagged to province, documents show
Students brace for debt, reconsider studies as OSAP cuts take effect

blocks.text: The instances of unusually rapid completion of courses warrants review, the Academy acknowledged, and said it has implemented additional monitoring of files before exam codes are issued.
"It's also important to note that time spent in our online learning platform is not, on its own, a complete measure of a student's learning," the Academy said in its statement.

"Students learn in different ways, some programs include third-party learning materials, and many students download textbooks and course materials to study off-line before completing their assessments. A short period of online activity or a quick assessment does not by itself mean the required learning did not take place."

articles.title: ARD-Deutschlandtrend survey: Germans unite in frustration over the government
articles.summary: On the 36th anniversary of reunification, Germans are dissatisfied with the country's political leaders. They don't believe they'll be able to handle the challenges posed by AI, Russia and Donald…

image.caption: SPD leader and Vice-Chancellor Lars Klingbeil (l) and CDU leader and Chancellor Friedrich Merz are feeling the mounting pressure on their governmentImage: Michael Kappeler/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ahead of October 3, which marks the reunification of West and East Germany in 1990, pollster infratest dimap asked 1303 eligible voters to assess their personal situation. Twenty percent of those identifying as East Germans, but 44% see personal advantages. Only a quarter said reunification had no major impact on them personally.

More than half of West German respondents said reunification had no major impact on their personal lives. The remaining half is split: 19% said reunification had a positive impact, while 18% said it had a negative one.

Germany held three state elections in September, two of them in eastern states. They were seen as a test of nationwide voter sentiment. The results were particularly devastating for the center-right Christian Democrats (CDU), the party of Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

In Saxony-Anhalt and the city-state of Berlin, where it had been in government, the CDU dropped by 10% compared to the previous election and lost its hold on power. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the party even failed to cross the 5% threshold for representation in parliament. This has never happened before in Germany's history.
Merz under pressure: CDU lawmaker on election setbacks
Chancellor Merz wants to remain in office

Merz has long been unpopular and has seen his support fall even further in the aftermath of the elections. The coalition he leads, comprised of the CDU, the conservative Christian Social Union (CSU) and the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), is unpopular. Only one in 10 respondents in the survey said they were satisfied with the federal government's work and the chancellor's performance, a historic low. Only 40% of CDU supporters say they are still satisfied with Merz.
Far-right AfD in the lead nationwide

The Alternative for Germany (AfD), which the domestic intelligence agency has classified as, in part, far-right extremist, continues to benefit from the voter dissatisfaction with the centrist parties.

If a general election were held now, the CDU/CSU alliance would win only 20% of the vote. That is one of the lowest figures in the party's history and a far cry from the 43.8% it won in the first election after reunification in 1990. The SPD polls at only 13%. This means that the ruling parties together would not even win one-third of the vote and would lose their majority in parliament.

The AfD would remain the strongest political force. It has been polling steadily at 27% nationwide. The environmentalist Greens are up slightly, reaching 16%, while the socialist Left Party has dropped by the same margin, landing at 11%. With this result, it would be a Herculean task to form a majority in the national parliament.
AI, Russia and Donald Trump's policies
The overall situation in Germany gives only one in eight people cause for optimism, while nearly nine in 10 express concern. Voters for the AfD and the Left Party are particularly worried.

Two-thirds of respondents said they're worried that humans could lose control over artificial intelligence, and just as many are worried about the consequences of US President Donald Trump's policies for Germany. Six in 10 expressed concern about climate change, and just over half said they are worried that Russia could attack other countries in Europe.
About one in two respondents fear they will not be able to maintain their standard of living in the future. A similar number are concerned about immigration to Germany.
By far the biggest source of concern for Germans, however, is that political parties cannot find common answers to key political issues.
Why Germany's political center is losing ground
Social reforms must be fair
Germany is a rapidly aging country. Fewer working people must support an ever-increasing number of retirees.

The aging society also strains the health care system. Since 2015, the number of people in need of long-term care has risen from about 2.8 million to about 6.5 million — and the trend continues to rise.
According to the ARD Deutschlandtrend survey, only one in six eligible voters believes that the federal government will succeed inmaking the social security systems sustainable for the future.

Not all respondents said they are willing to dig into their own pockets: Voters who tend to support left-leaning parties would be more likely to accept higher social security contributions than benefit cuts. Among AfD and CDU/CSU voters, the opposite is true.
Three-quarters of respondents view the government's proposed reform measures as contradictory. They complain about an ever-increasing burden, even though the government had promised relief.
What Germans young and old think about the pension system
Sixty-one percent say that cuts should be scaled according to individual financial capacity, even if this would place a heavier burden on some people.

One in two would be more willing to accept cuts if the necessity were explained in a way that made sense. The message to policymakers is clear: reforms require explanation and social balance; otherwise, they lose acceptance.

The welfare state and the health care system are regarded as key achievements in Germany. When asked what works particularly well in Germany compared to other countries, survey respondents most often cited social benefits and medical care. Education, schools, vocational training and universities came in last place.
Energy policy is seen as a problem

High energy prices continue to burden citizens and the German economy. The ongoing crisis in the Persian Gulf is driving oil prices even higher. This is impacting fuel and electricity prices in Germany.
Respondents to the ARD Deutschlandtrend survey found that the government is not doing enough to address high energy prices. Three-quarters of them said the government's efforts are insufficient.

A "Tankrabatt" (fuel discount) has again come into effect on October 1: Through the end of the year, the federal government is reducing the energy tax on gasoline and diesel by about 17 eurocents ($0.19) per liter. A similar discount was already in place from early May through the end of June. That cost the government €3.4 billion.
Some of that money ended up in the pockets of oil companies and gas station operators because they did not pass on the full discount. Experts view the measure critically.

Added to this is the fact that fossil fuels are being made cheaper despite shortages, which is controversial from a climate policy perspective. The new fuel discount has received only a lukewarm reception among the public; half of those surveyed in the ARD Deutschlandtrend poll believe it is the wrong approach.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.summary: Kathy Hochul said she no longer has faith in the local district attorney’s ability to handle the case, which has restarted a national conversation about sexual assault on college…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 28m agoNew York governor to provide update on Cornell gang-rape case after appointing special prosecutor

blocks.text: New York governor to provide update on Cornell gang-rape case after appointing special prosecutor

The governor of New York, Kathy Hochul, has named New York attorney general Letitia James as special prosecutor to investigate an alleged gang-rape at Cornell University in 2024, saying she had lost faith in the local district attorney’s ability to handle the case.
Both Hochul and James are due to speak today to provide an update on the investigation following the attorney general’s appointment.
Hochul said newly released information raised questions about the investigation conducted by Cornell police and the decision by Tompkins County prosecutors not to file charges.
“This has, in turn, undercut my faith, and the public’s faith, in the district attorney’s ability to effectively investigate and prosecute the case at this time,” she said in a statement.
James will oversee the investigation and, if warranted, present evidence to a grand jury, Hochul added.

blocks.caption: New York state attorney general Letitia James has been appointed as special prosecutor to look into an alleged gang-rape at Cornell University. Photograph: Brendan McDermid/Reuters

blocks.text: Matthew Van Houten, the Tompkins County district attorney, declined at the time of the alleged assault to file charges, saying his office chose not to prosecute because the victim’s testimony did not establish a lack of consent.
But with renewed attention on the case and mounting public pressure, Van Houten said on Monday that his office would reopen the investigation.

A woman, known as Jane Doe in court documents, filed a civil lawsuit last month alleging she had been drugged with ketamine and raped by a group of men at a fraternity house near Cornell University’s campus in October 2024. She reported the incident to the Cornell University police department several weeks later, but no criminal charges were filed.
James said her office would “fully and fairly” investigate the allegations.

articles.title: Trillanes to Escudero: Focus on evidence, not technicalities in Sara Duterte trial
articles.summary: Former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV urged Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero to prioritize the presentation of evidence over technicalities in the impeachment trial of Vice…

blocks.text: Published October 2, 2026 6:20pm

Former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV urged Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero to prioritize the presentation of evidence over technicalities in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Trillanes made the remarks a day after the prosecution dropped him from its list of witnesses. He later said he was the one who asked the prosecution to remove his name, saying he felt unwelcome before the Senate impeachment court after Escudero declined to issue him a subpoena.

“Iyong presiding officer lang naman ’yung nagtitimon. So kung boring ’yung impeachment trial, it’s the fault entirely of the presiding officer. Kapag tinrato mo itong parang criminal court, ganyan ang mangyayari,” Trillanes said.
(It is the presiding officer who calls the shots. If the impeachment trial becomes boring, that's on him. If you make it akin to a criminal court, that is what will happen.)

“Mahigit 30 na kaso na rin ang kinaharap ko eh. I have lived it; it can be boring talaga. But that should not be the case for the impeachment court. Dapat hinahanap nila 'yung katotohanan. Hindi naman ito criminal trial na may kulong," Trillanes added.
(I have faced around 30 cases myself, and the trial could get boring. But the impeachment court should search for the truth. This is not a criminal trial, where the punishment is jail time.)
Trillanes then reiterated his previous position that it should be Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian who should be the presiding officer for a more understandable approach on issues at hand.
“That is why I was pushing for Senator Sherwin as presiding officer because he has a layman mindset. But they were saying that it has to be a lawyer. No, we don’t need a lawyer here,” Trillanes said.
“Kailangan lang dito may bukas na pag-iisip na kailangan hanapin yung katotohanan. Ganoon lang po yun,” Trillanes added.
(What we need is someone who is willing to search for the truth. It is that simple.)

Trillanes cited the recent deferment of the presentation of Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura of the Anti-Money Laundering Council as a witness for the prosecution, with presiding officer Escudero granting the defense’s request for more time to prepare.

“Napagbotohan na nila ’yan. Nag-agree na sila diyan. Kung objective ang presiding officer, tapos na yan. Present niyo na yan. Tapos may kopya na sila. Kailangan [raw] nila (defense) ng oras. Parang sounds reasonable, right? Pero hawak na nila ‘yung mga dokumento na ’yon weeks before. Pero kinatigan sila ng presiding officer,” Trillanes said.

(They already voted on it that the presentation of AMLC, bank records are allowed. The witness from AMLC should have presented already. Both parties already have copies of these. The defense said they needed time. It sounds reasonable, but they already have the documents way back. And yet the presiding officer ruled in their favor.)
“E di nagsayang ng isa't kalahating araw. So bantayan nyo yung presiding officer. That's what I'm saying. Tingnan nyo. Kung boring, problema niya ‘yun,” Trillanes added.
(A day was wasted. So you should keep watch on the presiding officer. Observe keenly. If it gets boring, that's on him.)

The prosecution is presenting evidence for Article 2 of the impeachment case against the Vice President, which alleges unexplained wealth stemming from her purported failure to truthfully disclose her assets in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs) and to divest from businesses, as required of the President and Vice President under the Constitution. —LDF, GMA News

Baird, father of former NSW premier Mike Baird and journalist Julia Baird, helped win the Olympics for Sydney

  • Get our

blocks.text: Bruce Baird, a former federal Liberal MP and deputy leader of the party’s New South Wales branch, has died aged 84.
Baird, who also served as the NSW transport minister from 1988 to 1995, is the father of former state premier Mike Baird, the ABC journalist Julia Baird, and the marketing executive Steve Baird.
As a NSW minister, Baird was instrumental in lobbying for the 2000 Olympic Games to be based in Sydney. He then entered federal parliament as the member for Cook.
Baird retired before the 2007 election, when Scott Morrison won the seat and went on to become prime minister.
Morrison said Baird was “a giant, a mentor and a friend who celebrated and lived out his strong Christian faith, loved his family and served his country, his state and our community in the shire”.
“His achievements are significant, most notably the transforming effect he had on our home city of Sydney as the minister for Sydney’s successful Olympic bid. But there are many more.”
NSW Liberal leader, Kellie Sloane, said Baird was “driven by a strong sense of service, conviction, and compassion, earning the trust and respect of people regardless of their political affiliation”.
“Above all, Bruce was a devoted husband to his late wife Judy, and a proud father and grandfather.”
after newsletter promotion
In a statement, a NSW Liberal spokesperson offered its “deepest condolences on behalf of all members to his family at this difficult time”.
Baird was a passionate supporter of refugees and advocated on their behalf throughout his career.
While a Liberal MP, he opposed the Howard government’s mandatory detention of asylum seekers. After leaving office, he became a member of Kevin Rudd’s refugee resettlement advisory council.
In 2010, Baird criticised the reopening of Curtin detention centre in Western Australia to house asylum seekers.
“Don’t confuse treating people badly when they arrive with effective border control mechanisms, they are two different things,” he told the ABC.
“If we rely on treating asylum seekers badly in this country then there is something about us that we need to have a hard look at. I don’t believe that is the Australian way.”
Baird was also a regular feature of Manly’s Bold and Beautiful ocean swimming club. A member of the squad also confirmed his death on Friday.
On Thursday, the club’s organiser, Peter Anthony, wrote to members describing Baird as a “wonderful friend to so many of us”.

articles.title: OpenAI disclose another hack on government department in Australia
articles.summary:
Attack accessing historical data on bushfires occurred in June but not disclosed by the tech company until Thursday

  • Get our

blocks.text: Artificial intelligence company OpenAI has disclosed another unauthorised hack on a government department in Australia.
In June, an OpenAI agent hacked into a New South Wales state government department and accessed historical non-public data on bushfires without authorisation.
The breach, which comes weeks after news of a similar hack on a federal government department involving Medicare data, was not reported by the US based company until Thursday.
The NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water is now working with the state’s cyber security agency to investigate the breach.
The Australian Signals Directorate has also been informed of the hack on the NSW national parks and wildlife service.
OpenAI told the NSW government that its agent had operated beyond its intended use and the statistics it obtained were not publicly available.
The company first became aware of the breach on Tuesday and conducted a 48 hours review to determine its scope before informing the NSW premier’s office.
“The results we reviewed do not show that the model retrieved any personal information,” an OpenAI spokesperson said.
This latest breach has added to calls for tougher regulation of AI companies and for bolstered cyber security defences.
“We simply cannot trust these companies. They have no respect for the sovereignty of our governments, of our way of life,” Greens MP Abigail Boyd said.
Boyd said it was damning that the breach occurred in June but the government was not notified until this week.

“We clearly cannot rely on these multinational big tech companies to comply with even the most minimal of social obligations such as notifying when, or even taking enough care to notice if, their products are hacking government systems,” Boyd said.
On Wednesday, the department of home affairs on Wednesday told federal departments to examine their older software and ensure cyber security was up to date.
The prime minister expressed his “extreme concern” about at an OpenAI agent hacking Australian Institute of Health and Welfare in June.
The Victorian Department of Health and the New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research were also compromised by an OpenAI agent.
An artificial intelligence agent is a system that autonomously solves problems, makes decisions, plans and performs complex tasks on behalf of another user or system, using all available tools.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Raffy Tulfo not arrested
articles.summary: Senator Raffy Tulfo was present at the Senate impeachment court days after YouTube videos falsely claimed he had been arrested

blocks.text: Claim: An arrest warrant was issued against Senator Raffy Tulfo, who was then apprehended by the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP).
Why we fact-checked this: The thumbnail of the YouTube video bearing the claim shows Tulfo alongside an image of a purported Supreme Court (SC) warrant and armed personnel from the AFP.
As of writing, the video posted on September 26 has 143,511 views, 3,800 likes, and 284 comments. Text on its thumbnail and its title read: “Raffy Tulfo may warrant! Utos ng Supreme Court sa AFP?”
(Raffy Tulfo has a warrant! Supreme Court order to the AFP?)

Another YouTube video uploaded by the same user on September 24 has 71,559 views, 2,300 likes, and 183 comments as of writing. Its thumbnail and caption state: “Raffy Tulfo inaresto ng AFP! Pinasok ang Senado?”
(Raffy Tulfo arrested by the AFP! Entered the Senate?)

The facts: Tulfo has not been arrested, and he continues to perform his duties as senator. No credible news reports, official notices from government agencies, or statements from Tulfo himself indicate that such an event happened.

Contrary to the claim, videos and live coverage show that he was present on Day 31 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on September 29, days after the first video claimed he had allegedly been arrested.

Neither YouTube video presents evidence of a warrant, court order, or any other official notice to support the claim. Instead, both contain unrelated political commentary on corruption, confidential funds, and voting in the 2028 elections.

Supposed SC warrant: The video does not identify any case that would have led to the issuance of an alleged arrest warrant against Tulfo. For a warrant to be issued, a case must first be filed before the proper court, after which trial court judges or justices determine whether probable cause exists to issue a warrant of arrest. (READ: Indicted? Charged? A guide to court jargon)
The Supreme Court primarily exercises original jurisdiction over certain cases and the authority to review, revise, modify, or affirm lower court decisions.

Publicly available Supreme Court records reviewed as of September 30 show no issuance that supports the claim. There are likewise no reports from credible media outlets about a warrant of arrest against Tulfo or his supposed arrest.
Tulfo’s role in Duterte’s impeachment trial: The false claim began circulating while Tulfo was serving as a senator-judge in the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

As a senator-judge, Tulfo previously questioned defense lawyer Michael Poa’s role as Duterte’s counsel, citing a potential conflict of interest following the relevation that Poa — previously an undersecretary and chief of staff of the Department of Education — had met with the Commission on Audit to discuss an audit query related to confidential funds.
Tulfo has also made statements about the Vice President’s alleged business involvements.

He was also among the 13 senator-judges who voted to lower the conviction threshold to 14 votes. His brother, senator-judge Erwin Tulfo, made the motion to bar absentee senators from voting in the trial.
Debunked: Rappler has previously fact-checked false claims about the Tulfo brothers:

FACT CHECK: Tulfo remains a sitting senator
FACT CHECK: Tulfo not suspended from Senate

blocks.text: – Agatha Gonzalvo/Rappler.com
Agatha Gonzalvo is a Research and Data volunteer intern at Rappler. She is a fourth-year Applied Economics student at De La Salle University Manila.

articles.title: 'I am Jane Doe': Online rally to protect Cornell rape accuser's identity becomes a reckoning

image.caption: Screen grabs of 'I am Jane Doe' social media posts by, from left, the parenting account Big Little Feelings, author G. Marino, and content creator @mylee_may_aez, posted Sept. 30 and Oct. 1, 2026. (@biglittlefeelings/Instagram, @gmarinoauthor/Instagram, @mylee_may_aez/TikTok)

blocks.text: World·New

The repeated refrain, part of an online wave of support this week for the complainant in the Cornell University gang rape allegations, is being compared to the cultural and structural reckoning of the 2017 #MeToo movement.
It's being compared to the 2017 #MeToo movement
WARNING: This article references sexual assault and may affect those who have experienced​ ​​​sexual violence or know someone affected by it.
They're saying it in videos posted on TikTok in solidarity, in Instagram posts where they hope to protect her identity, and in comments on Threads where they share their own harrowing experiences:
"I am Jane Doe."

The repeated refrain, part of a wave of online support this week for the complainant in the Cornell University gang-rape allegations, is being compared to the cultural and structural reckoning of the 2017 #MeToo movement that changed the culture of silence around sexual assault.

The Cornell case recently came under the spotlight after the complainant, known in court documents as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit on Sept. 16 alleging the Ivy League university protected the seven men, now dubbed "the Cornell 7."

The #iamjanedoe movement seems to have been born out of an attempt to protect Jane Doe's identity after an independent journalist put out a public call Monday to name her "so we can all evaluate her veracity ... since her lawsuit didn't hesitate to name and shame seven of her peers as gang-rapists."
He later claimed to have identified her, posting and then deleting her information, adding "the principle has been served."
The global response across the internet was swift.
"He is trying to expose her identity. We won't let him. I am Jane Doe," a content creator posted in a video on TikTok viewed more than 5.2 million times by Friday.
"You are Jane Doe, I am Jane Doe, we are ALL Jane Doe until no one is Jane Doe," someone else commented.
"We all are Jane Doe, good luck finding her, men," another person commented on one user's Instagram video.

Jane Doe alleges the men named in her lawsuit plied her with ketamine and assaulted her over several hours at a frat house in October 2024. None of the fraternity members have been criminally charged. On Monday, after intense backlash, the Tompkins County district attorney announced he was reopening the investigation.
By Thursday evening, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said she’d lost faith in the DA's ability to handle the case and was appointing New York attorney general Letitia James to oversee the investigation.

On Friday, Hochul says she intends to "close the loophole" in her state's law that currently makes it difficult for sexual assault survivors to claim they were mentally incapacitated during an assault if they were voluntarily intoxicated.
New York governor says 'I want the truth' in Cornell case
'It's happening all the time'

There are currently thousands of online "I am Jane Doe" posts across multiple platforms, reaching millions of people. And while one of the goals is to bury any identifying information of the actual Jane Doe, it is also a moment of reckoning.
Many of the posters have been describing their own sexual assault experiences, the difficulties in coming forward and, in some cases, naming the people they say harmed them.

items: What Cornell's alleged rape case and the Hockey Canada trial's striking parallels reveal
What to know about Cornell's alleged frat house gang-rape case and the 'Cornell 7'

blocks.text: "Four men at once. I was 22," someone posted on TikTok.
"I was 18," someone posted on Instagram.
"People need to realize this is happening to so many women, not just one brave woman at Cornell University. It’s happening all the time. Everywhere to SOOO MANY women," she added.

In Canada, about 44 per cent of the population over age 15 say they have been sexually assaulted in their lifetime, with women three times as likely to say so as men, according to a 2025 survey by Statistics Canada. Fewer than one in 10 reported it to the police.
According to the U.S. Rape, Abuse and Incest National Network (RAINN), about one in four undergraduate women experience rape or sexual assault after enrolling in college.
'We are so damn tired'
U.S. journalist Katie Couric gathered some of the responses she'd seen online and posted them on Threads on Wednesday.
"The Cornell case has unleashed a torrent of first-person accounts from women revisiting traumatic experiences they had long kept buried," Couric wrote.

They included posts by one user who said they'd been assaulted by their professor, who was allowed to retire early and is now a dean at another school. Another said they'd been raped while asleep, still another said they had been drugged and raped for hours on a college campus while people watched and nobody was prosecuted.
"It feels like shouting into a void," someone commented. "It's infuriating."
The feeling was echoed on Substack, where an author asked what's really changed since #MeToo.

"The viral #MeToo movement in 2017 felt so significant because it was the largest collective reckoning of rape culture maybe ever, and happened mostly in an online space. It was the first time I said things out loud that I had kept to myself for most of my life," she wrote in a post Tuesday.
"The same is happening now with the Cornell 7, but we are almost 10 years on from #MeToo and we are so damn tired."

If you’re in immediate danger or fear for your safety or that of others around you, please call 911. For support in your area, you can look for crisis lines and local services via the Ending Sexual Violence Association of Canada database. ​​
'Cornell 7' lawsuit: What we know
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Natalie Stechyson has been a writer and editor at CBC News since 2021. She covers stories on social trends, families, gender, human interest, as well as general news. She's worked as a journalist since 2009, with stints at the Globe and Mail and Postmedia News, among others. Before joining CBC News, she was the parents editor at HuffPost Canada, where she won a silver Canadian Online Publishing Award for her work on pregnancy loss. You can reach her at natalie.stechyson@cbc.ca.

October 2, 2026
Union slams VW over scrapping labor agreements
Germany's IG Metall union has sharply criticized Volkswagen over its latest cost-cutting drive, accusing management of provoking a conflict "that the company cannot afford."

Thorsten Gröger, IG Metall's regional head for Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt, told public broadcaster Deutschlandfunk that VW's approach was "disrespectful toward its own employees" and "irresponsible toward the company itself."

Gröger said worker representatives had listened to a 50-minute presentation from management without hearing "a single word" about plans to terminate key collective bargaining agreements, while the media had already been informed.
He described the move as "unprecedented in the history of Volkswagen" and said employee representatives were prepared for the dispute.
VW says employment conditions need to be revised because of mounting cost pressures.
The carmaker plans to cut 50,000 jobs worldwide in the coming years, on top of previously announced reductions. Around half of the additional cuts could come in Germany.
The longer-term future of entire VW plants in Emden, Hannover and Zwickau, as well as Audi's Neckarsulm site, also remains uncertain.

articles.title: 'I was fighting for my life': Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls FlyDubai cockpit attack
articles.summary: The Indian airline captain who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a FlyDubai flight described Friday how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane…

image.caption: Capt. Smit Machchhar, who is from Mumbai, was seriously injured in Wednesday's attack but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and restrain the attacker. (Israel's Foreign Ministry/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

The Indian airline captain who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a FlyDubai flight described Friday how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent.
Capt. Smit Machchhar spoke to Indian PM in interview broadcast live from hospital

Capt. Smit Machchhar, recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a video call broadcast live on television news channels that he knew he had to get back on his feet to save the passengers aboard the aircraft.
"I had so many wounds. I had fallen down," he said from the hospital, his head bandaged and tubes in his nose, before breaking down as he recalled the attack.
"I was fighting for my life. At one point, I realized that if I didn't get up … then passengers would lose their lives," he told Modi.

items: Passengers foil bid to crash Dubai-Tel Aviv flight after co-pilot stabbed pilot, Israel says
What we know so far about the midair FlyDubai attack

blocks.text: Machchhar, who is from India's financial hub of Mumbai, was seriously injured in Wednesday's attack but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and restrain the attacker as the Boeing 737 descended sharply, witnesses and Israeli authorities said.
He has been hailed as a hero for his actions, with world leaders saying he helped prevent a potential disaster.
Indian FlyDubai pilot hailed as hero in Mumbai
The flight, carrying 182 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was diverted to Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia for an emergency landing.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attacker, an Omani national, was arrested in Saudi Arabia and was undergoing interrogation there. His motive for the attack was not immediately clear.
Recited prayer for strength
Machchhar said that during those difficult moments, he recited the Hanuman Chalisa, a Hindu devotional hymn dedicated to Lord Hanuman and traditionally recited as a prayer for strength and courage.
"Lord Hanuman gave me courage," he told Modi.

Machchhar, who is married and has two children, has worked for FlyDubai for about four years, according to his LinkedIn profile. Before joining the airline, he spent 11 years with SpiceJet, an Indian low-cost carrier, where he served as a senior commander and line training captain. He logged more than 9,750 flying hours with SpiceJet.
