articles.title: Ukraine: Kyiv bridges shut after fatal Russian drone assault
articles.summary: The latest Russian attacks killed at least one person and severely disrupted traffic in the Ukrainian capital. Several bridges over the Dnipro River connect western and eastern Kyiv.

image.caption: The Pivdennyi Bridge, or Southern Bridge, was one of the bridges closed as a result of the latest Russian drone attack [FILE: April 19, 2019]Image: Christophe Gateau/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Several bridges in Kyiv have been closed as the result of new Russian drone attacks which killed one person in the city, the Ukrainian capital's authorities said Friday.
There are a total of eight bridges that connect Kyiv's western and eastern banks along the Dnipro River.
What do we know about the Russian drone attack on Kyiv?
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city's Southern Bridge, also known as the Pivdennyi Bridge, was "completely closed" to traffic.

blocks.caption: A Russian strike hit a building in the Darnytskyi District in southeastern Kyiv Image: Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS

blocks.text: The concrete and steel bridge carries road vehicles and a metro rail line. The Southern Bridge has been hit twice over the two days by Russian drone attacks.
The Paton Bridge was also closed to traffic towards the left bank of the Dnipro River, Klitschko said.

Russia's Ministry of Defense said its drones targeted a bridge over the Dnipro which is used for military purposes. Russia also said it attacked a power station in the surrounding Kyiv region alongside the Port of Izmail near the Black Sea and a cargo vessel.
A Russian attack on Kyiv also left one person in dead and at least two others injured after a strike hit a 25-story building in the Darnytskyi district.

Russia has frequently targeted Kyiv with overnight drone attacks in the years since the start of the February 2022 invasion. Ukraine in response has been developing interceptor technology to down those combat drones.

blocks.caption: Residents in Kyiv are frequently terrorized by nightly Russian drone attacks Image: Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS

blocks.text: Ukraine carries out fresh attacks on Russian oil facilities

Meanwhile, the governor of Russia's southern Volgograd region said Ukrainian drone attacks targeted industrial infrastructure. An apartment building was also damaged in the Ukrainian attack, wounding one person.
Authorities in the southern Russian region of Krasnodar said drone debris damaged an "enterprise" in the Black Sea city of Tuapse.
In a post on X, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces carried out attacks over the past 24 hours on oil facilities in the Samara and Volgograd regions.

"Successful operations were carried out in the Black Sea and in the Voronezh, Nizhny Novgorod, Volgograd, Samara and Krasnodar regions, targeting airfields, industrial facilities, oil refineries, a missile and space center, and an ammunition depot belonging to the occupiers," Zelenskyy said.
Ukraine's military has been targeting oil refineries in Russia over the past year in an attempt to cripple the country's energy industry.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said Thursday that Russia has lost 1% of GDP due to the Ukrainian strikes.

articles.title: France: 400 schools closed as student protests continue
articles.summary: Police have made around 2,000 arrests and scores of people have been injured as student protests spread across France. Ministers have called for a "day of dialogue" but students have called for…

image.caption: "Protest is a fundamental right," reads one placard. "You don't want to hear our words; you just fire tear gas," reads another.Image: Sarah Meyssonnier/REUTERS

blocks.text: Over 400 schools and colleges across France remained closed on Friday as student protests over education-related grievances continued — with some turning violent.

"There are over ⁠400 schools and other educational establishments that I know of that will be closed," confirmed French Education ​Minister Edouard Geffray on broadcaster ​France 2 late on Thursday night.

The protests ​against teacher shortages, dilapidated school buildings and a lack of learning materials erupted at lycées (equivalent to US high schools) in the Paris region last month before spreading across the country this week.

blocks.caption: Students are angry at what they see as a general lack of investment in their educationImage: Abdul Saboor/REUTERS

blocks.text: Student protests in France: damage, injuries, arrests
Police have made around 2,000 arrests and scores of people have been injured, including 40 high school principals, according to Geffray.
Fires were started in at least two high schools on Thursday, while teachers were reportedly inadvertently ​splashed with petrol ⁠at a third in the southern city of Marseille, according to officials.
At ​least one car was torched in the eastern city of Strasbourg while riot police clashed with youths in Toulouse in the southwest.
In the southeastern region of Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, authorities claimed that "at least €25 million" of damage has been done in their jurisdiction alone.
On Friday, more clashes between student protesters and police were reported in cities across the country, including in Loire, where several officers were injured, and in the capital Paris.
But students have also criticized what they see as a heavy-handed police response.
"You don't want to hear our words; you just fire tear gas," one student wrote on a placard outside the Lycée Voltaire in central Paris (see main photo above).
"Protest is a fundamental right," read another sign.
France students protest school conditions

Minister Geffray told broadcasters on Friday morning that "violent individuals" were "infiltrating groups of students" and "taking the movement hostage" and called on parents to prevent their children from joining the protests.
"What matters now is ensuring our children are no longer out on the streets, because they are in danger," he said.
Geffray was planning to meet with student representatives and trade unions on Friday, saying: "Today will be a day of dialogue."
France: government blames far-left LFI

According to Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, French domestic intelligence agencies told a crisis meeting on Thursday that the movement has been initiated by politicians from the left-wing party La France Insoumise (France Unbowed or LFI) – who have denied the allegations.
Veteran LFI leader and 2027 presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon has indeed supported the protests but called on students to use non-violent methods.

"Students, teachers and educational staff are facing the same state of neglect and their positions and claims should be respected," he wrote in a statement earlier this week, calling for "disciplined struggle, no panic, no irritation."
Meanwhile, student union bodies have called for a day of mass protest next Tuesday, October 6, under the slogan: "Police out of schools! No to the repression of student mobilization!"
"The police have no place in front of educational establishments," read a statement. "We support the ongoing mobilization and call for it to be reinforced."

articles.title: Trillanes unwelcome? A baseless assumption, says impeachment court spox
articles.summary: Former senator Sonny Trillanes claiming that he was not welcome to the Senate impeachment court is a “baseless assumption,” spokesperson Atty. Regie Tongol said Friday.

blocks.text: Published October 2, 2026 5:02pm
Former senator Sonny Trillanes claiming that he was not welcome to the Senate impeachment court is a “baseless assumption,” spokesperson Atty. Regie Tongol said Friday.

“Wala po, kasi wala naman pong ganyang pakiwari ang impeachment court at senator-judges kay former senator Trillanes. In fact, the fact na nakapasok nga siya nung Tuesday na nandun po siya at nakaupo po siya doon sa aming gallery kung saan ay nakalaan po iyon sa mga very important persons,” Tongol said in a press briefing.

(There is none, there is no sentiment like that from the impeachment court and the senator-judges regarding former senator Trillanes. The fact that he was able to come in last Tuesday and was able to sit in the gallery, which is designated for very important persons.)
“Walang ganoon na pinakita sa kanya ang impeachment court so I think that would be a baseless assumption kasi we have to base everything on the actions of the court,” he added.
(The impeachment court did not show anything like that to him so I think that would be a baseless assumption because we have to base everything on the actions of the court.)
Trillanes was among those named by the prosecution as their witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte but the impeachment court did not issue a subpoena for him.

The House prosecution panel said Thursday that they will no longer present the former senator as witness. Later in the day, Trillanes said it was he who asked the prosecution panel to withdraw his name
In a press conference Friday, Trillanes questioned why the impeachment court did not issue him a subpoena to testify for the prosecution.

"Sa akin kasi the signal is clear, hindi ako welcome. And by the way, hindi ito collective na parang sinasabi kasi ayaw daw ako ng mga senador. Inisa-isa natin 'yung mga naabutan natin doon. Hindi naman sila nakonsulta kaya next time na may magsabi na kasi may mga ano yung mga senador, don't swallow it right away,” he added.

(For me, the signal is clear: I was not welcome, but this is not a collective sentiment. There were comments that senators do not like me. I asked my former colleagues, and they said they weren’t consulted. So next time someone says senators don’t like me, don’t swallow it right away.)

Tongol explained that last Monday, Trillanes was supposed to be issued a subpoena. When the prosecution was asked who was going to be issued a subpoena, House prosecutor Terry Ridon did not mention the former senator.
The day after that, the prosecution mentioned that they wanted Trillanes to take a seat, but impeachment presiding officer Chiz Escudero could not issue a subpoena for the next day.
However, they could still have Trillanes as a voluntary witness. The presiding officer then warned the prosecution that they may be putting the cart before the horse, according to Tongol.
“Wala pa naman, at that time, na humingi sila na uupo na si former senator Trillanes, wala pang nape-presentang bank records noong panahon na 'yun, nung Tuesday,” Tongol said.
(At the time they were asking for former senator Trillanes to take a seat, no bank record has been presented yet.)
Tongol welcomed any criticisms from Trillanes regarding the court’s handling of the impeachment process, saying it is his freedom to do so. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Row erupts over Cairo mural depicting Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin
articles.summary:
Artwork created in Tahrir Square for Chinese president’s state visit to Egypt is painted over amid allegations it revived Afrocentric claims about Pharaohs’ origins

On the…

blocks.text: On the eve of Chinese president Xi Jinping’s state visit to Cairo last month, the city authorities were busy removing a 66-metre-long mural from the esteemed guest’s line of sight.

Depicting the Pharaoh Tutankhamun and Queen Nefertiti, the painting was among 40 murals commissioned to beautify the city for Xi’s arrival and was painted by volunteer youth group Rasmet Basma, in Tahrir Square.

But it drew a furious reaction for depicting the two historical figures with dark skin – angering those Egyptians who saw it as reviving Afrocentric claims about the Pharaohs’ origins. The artwork vanished under fresh paint just hours before Xi landed.
Now, Ahmed Moussa, the 22-year-old founder of Rasmet Basma, has admitted it was asked by the Cairo governorate to paint over its work, which had been prepared in just five days in late August.

blocks.caption: Volunteer Razan Mujahid works on the mural. Photograph: Rasmet Basma

blocks.text: The team used the AI programme ChatGPT to generate the designs, which volunteers then painted on to the wall.
Moussa said Cairo’s deputy governor and the head of the district had visited the site throughout the process and were impressed by the murals – until controversy began to build on social media.
“We used a golden-bronze tone that cast a kind of shadow on the faces at night, so they appeared dark-skinned,” Moussa said.
“We acknowledge our mistake in not consulting specialists in archaeology and art.”
Afrocentrism is a political movement asserting that ancient Egyptian civilisation was black African in origin and population.

One user asked whether anyone involved had “even seen what Nefertiti actually looked like”, while others accused Afrocentric groups of appropriating the images to claim Egyptians endorsed their theories.

Zahi Hawass, Egypt’s former antiquities minister, said the volunteers should not have been allowed to paint a city site as significant as Tahrir Square without expert oversight, and that the public outrage was justified.
“Claims linking ancient Egyptian civilisation to sub-Saharan Africa are nonsense,” Hawass said.
“Temple carvings from the late period show Egyptian kings depicted alongside captives from parts of Africa, Libya, Syria and Palestine, with the king himself not shown as dark-skinned,” he said.

blocks.caption: The mural has reignited a debate about the complexion of ancient Egyptians. Photograph: Rasmet Basma

blocks.text: This is just the latest episode in a long-running debate over the complexion of ancient Egyptians. In 2023, a Netflix documentary provoked discussion after casting a dark-skinned actor as Cleopatra, and a similar dispute flared in June 2024 after a guide reportedly gave an Afrocentric perspective of Egyptian history in Cairo’s Egyptian Museum.

Monica Hanna, an Egyptologist at the American University in Cairo, labelled Afrocentric claims “pseudoscience”. She said Egyptian society had always been ethnically diverse, from Nubian communities in the south to Mediterranean populations in the north.
“Egyptians were never one skin colour,” she said. “We are not snow-white, or the colour of cream.”

Walid Mahmoud, an AI researcher and expert in African anthropology, said AI tools such as ChatGPT reflected whatever information was most widely shared online, rather than what was factually accurate.
They were built by companies in the US and Europe, he said, and the content they generated could shape how those audiences saw themselves.

blocks.caption: The mural was repainted white just hours before President Xi landed in Egypt. Photograph: Hanaa Hammad

blocks.text: “That’s why we should never simply accept what it produces, especially when it comes to cultural identity and heritage,” Mahmoud said.
Mostafa Eissa, an art critic, said AI should remain a tool, never a decision-maker in its own right.

“I favour using technology without abandoning the human element within the artist,” he said, warning that letting such tools substitute an artist’s own skill risked emptying a work of its originality.

articles.title: Senate bill eyes to lower age for SK voting, candidacy to 15-21 years old
articles.summary: From 18 to 24 years old, the proposed measure seeks to lower the age requirement to 15 to 21 years old.

blocks.text: People gesture after casting their votes during the presidential election at a polling station in Manila on May 9, 2022.
AFP / Chaideer Mahyuddin
MANILA, Philippines — A measure seeking to lower the age of eligible voters and candidates for Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) is being pushed in the Senate.

Senate Bill No. 2510 introduced by Sen. Vicente ‘Tito’ Sotto III is pushing to lower the age of young adults who are eligible to vote and run for positions in barangay’s youth council by amending Section 10 of the Republic Act No. 10742 or the Sangguniang Kabataan Reform Act of 2015.
From 18 to 24 years old, the proposed measure seeks to lower the age requirement to 15 to 21 years old.
In the bill’s explanatory note, Sotto said there is a need to bring back the SK mechanism to the youth sector and noted the importance of teaching children good governance.
“They are the voice and the representation of the youth in our governance framework, especially to the unit of government that is closest to the people,” Sotto said.

The bill comes a week after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. approved Republic Act No. 12326 which postponed the supposed barangay and SK elections on November 2 this year, moving it to the first Monday of November 2028.
No hard infra projects

Sotto’s proposed measure is also seeking to prohibit the SK funds to be used for procurement of hard infrastructure projects and high value properties that are higher than one-fourths of their annual budget.

“The Sangguniang Kabataan shall be prohibited from participating and their funds shall not be utilized in the procurement of hard infrastructure projects and high value properties where the amount of which exceeds 25% of their annual budget,” the proposed additional paragraph on Section 20 of Republic Act No. 10742 read.

The proposed additional paragraph, moreover, says the development plan of the youth council shall be strictly followed in the procurement process, saying any goods or properties not indicated in the plan shall not be purchased “unless a notarized justification in writing is submitted.”

“This bill aims to lower the age of qualification to run in the Sangguniang Kabataan and provide mechanisms that will deter corrupt practices and to allow the youth to be developed as effective leaders and to lead their fellow youth through the Sanggunian,” Sotto said.
Amendments on SK functions
Aside from lowering the age of eligible voters and officers, the bill is also pushing amendments related to SK funds and functions.

Sotto is seeking to limit the scope of plans and programs indicated in the Comprehensive Barangay Youth Development Plan, or the three-year rolling plan that the youth council must develop upon their assumption in office.

“The plans and programs to be indicated therein shall be limited to advocacy and campaigns, information and education, sports and physical development, welfare and support systems, and such other programs geared towards supporting the youth within their jurisdiction,” the proposed amendment read.

Plans and programs, it added, shall focus on good governance, climate change adaptation and environmental protection, disaster risk reduction, health services, anti-drug abuse, gender sensitivity, sports development, accessible education, sustainable development, human rights advocacy, and social protection.

articles.title: ‘I was fighting for my life’: Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls flydubai cockpit attack
articles.summary:
Smit Machchhar says in video call with Indian PM that he realised if he did not get up then ‘passengers would lose their lives’

The Indian pilot who helped thwart an

blocks.text: The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight has described how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent.

Capt Smit Machchhar, who is recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, told the Indian prime minister, Narendra Modi, in a video call broadcast live on television news channels that he knew he had to get back on his feet to save the passengers onboard.
“I had so many wounds. I had fallen down,” he said on Friday from the hospital, his head bandaged and tubes in his nose, before breaking down as he recalled the attack.
“I was fighting for my life. At one point, I realised that if I didn’t get up … then passengers would lose their lives,” he told Modi.

Machchhar, who is from Mumbai, was seriously injured in Wednesday’s attack but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and restrain the attacker as the Boeing 737 descended sharply, witnesses and Israeli authorities said. He has been hailed as a hero for his actions, with world leaders saying he helped prevent a potential disaster.
The flight, carrying 182 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was diverted to Tabuk in north-western Saudi Arabia for an emergency landing.
The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, said the attacker, an Omani national, was arrested in Saudi Arabia and was undergoing interrogation there. His motive for the attack remains unclear.

Machchhar said that during the difficult moments, he recited the Hanuman Chalisa, a devotional hymn dedicated to the Hindu deity Hanuman and traditionally recited as a prayer for strength and courage.
“Lord Hanuman gave me courage,” he told Modi.

Machchhar, who is married and has two children, has worked for flydubai for about four years, according to his LinkedIn profile. Before joining the airline, he spent 11 years with SpiceJet, an Indian low-cost carrier, where he served as a senior commander and line training captain. He logged more than 9,750 flying hours with SpiceJet.

articles.title: Who’s behind Trillanes’ trial withdrawal? He won’t say Escudero, but calls him out
articles.summary: Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV doesn't explicitly disclose what he means when he says the prosecution is being pressured over his testimony, but he still can't resist taking a swipe at the…

blocks.text: SPEAKING OUT. Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV holds a press conference at Club Filipino in San Juan City on October 2, 2026, where he presented his findings on the alleged ill-gotten wealth of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Jire Carreon/Rappler

Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV doesn't explicitly disclose what he means when he says the prosecution is being pressured over his testimony, but he still can't resist taking a swipe at the trial's presiding officer
Listening to former senator Antonio Trillanes IV’s press conference is an exercise in reading between the lines.

Trillanes, fresh from his removal from the prosecution’s witness lineup in Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial, consistently faced questions from the media on the identity of the individuals who orchestrated his eventual withdrawal.
The veteran politician dodged these questions over and over, yet in the same breath repeatedly took a swipe at one person: presiding officer Chiz Escudero.
At first, Trillanes didn’t want to give reporters a juicy soundbite on the “pressure” subject.

“I would have wanted to address that, but it would be a distraction from the main issue that we want to discuss, which is more important,” Trillanes said in Filipino on Friday, October 2. When asked if the pressure was coming from the senator-judges, he quipped, “No comment.”
Relentless journalists didn’t drop the subject, prompting Trillanes to eventually take a swipe at Escudero, without explicitly naming him.

“It’s this simple: The prosecution requested that certain people be subpoenaed. My name was on the list. The subpoenas came back, and I was the only one missing. Does the impeachment court have that kind of power? Does the presiding officer have the power to say, ‘Not this one yet’? That is the question. They don’t have that power. Because this is the prosecution’s strategy,” Trillanes said.
“Let us suspend our judgment, but let’s call him out,” he added.

blocks.caption: Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV holds a press conference at Club Filipino in San Juan City on October 2, 2026, where he presented his findings on the alleged ill-gotten wealth of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: For the record, Escudero had suggested that the prosecution present witnesses from the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) and the banks first in their unexplained wealth case against the Vice President before calling Trillanes to the witness stand.

It was a peculiar week of the trial at the Senate, though, marred by a sudden cancellation of a trial day, deferment of the presentation of the AMLC witness, and lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro’s abrupt withdrawal of Trillanes’ name from its lineup, to the surprise of even some of her colleagues in the panel, based on our candid conversations with them.

Letting go of Trillanes has its pros and cons for the prosecution and even the former senator. It’s a risky move to present a witness who has a fraught history with senator-judges, although his testimony would have been potentially explosive and highly interesting to the general public.

blocks.caption: 5 explosive allegations from Trillanes after impeachment trial withdrawal

blocks.text: For Trillanes, a court appearance may have limited what he could actually say due to — as he points out — the constant objections by the defense team. He argued the objections were unnecessary and could have been stopped by Escudero himself.

“If the person presiding over that were competent, the presentation of evidence should be liberal. Because what you want is the truth. This isn’t a criminal trial where someone gets sent to jail,” Trillanes said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Dive into Spanish cinema (and more) with this year’s ‘Película>Pelikula’ lineup
articles.summary: No Spanish fluency required! Find your next watch based on your mood, interests, and the kind of story you want to see

blocks.text: You know that feeling when you’re itching to watch a movie, but end up spending 30 minutes scrolling through your streaming platform instead? Now, imagine having 23 movies to choose from – in the cinema, on top of that.

Welcome to PELÍCULA>PELIKULA, a celebration of the 25 years of the Manila Spanish Film Festival. This year’s edition brings together films from Spain, Latin America, and the Philippines that range from dramas and documentaries to animation, comedy, and shorts.

Running October 4 to 11, you can catch the (free!) screenings at Instituto Cervantes Intramuros on October 4 and Power Plant Cinema 2 from October 5 to 11. Films are shown in their original languages and with English subtitles.
If 23 titles feel like homework, here’s your cheat sheet: pick a film based on what you’re in the mood for.

Start with Los domingos (2025), a Spanish drama directed by Alauda Ruiz de Azúa. The film follows 17-year-old Ainara, whose life and beliefs are thrown into question, making it a good pick if you like coming-of-age stories that leave you with something to think about after the credits.
The film is also one of the most recognized titles in this year’s lineup, earning the most nominations at Spain’s 40th Goya Awards.

Another option is Maspalomas (2025), which explores identity, aging, and the possibility of starting over. The film is part of the festival’s Premios Goya on Tour, a special selection of seven recent Spanish productions presented in partnership with the Spanish Film Academy.

The Room Next Door (La habitación de al lado) follows Ingrid and Martha, two old friends who reconnect after years apart. As they spend time together, they find themselves confronting illness, complicated relationships, and difficult choices.

Directed by Pedro Almodóvar, the film stars Julianne Moore and Tilda Swinton and is part of the festival’s Goya-focused selection. And if you’ve never seen an Almodóvar film before, this could be a good place to start.

blocks.caption: Dive into Spanish cinema (and more) with this year’s ‘Película>Pelikula’ lineup

blocks.text: For a more visceral movie night, try Sirāt, directed by Oliver Laxe.

The film follows a father and his son as they search for the son’s missing sister in Morocco, eventually becoming involved with a group of ravers traveling through the desert. It is one of the seven Goya titles in the festival and was among the most-nominated films at the 40th Goya Awards.
If that darker mood is what you’re after, keep going with Los Tigres, directed by Alberto Rodríguez, another Goya selection.

blocks.caption: Dive into Spanish cinema (and more) with this year’s ‘Película>Pelikula’ lineup

blocks.text: L’Olívia i el terratrèmol invisible (Olivia and the Invisible Earthquake) brings 12-year-old Olivia into a new neighborhood after her family is forced to leave their home. With the help of friends and a little adventure, she learns to navigate a major change in her life.
For a story filled with action and fantasy, Gigantes: una aventura extraordinaria brings three friends together on a mission to save their town from a devastating storm.
Both are part of La Previa, a four-film marathon kicking off on October 4 at Instituto Cervantes Intramuros, alongside Mensaje en una botella and Mariposas negras.

blocks.caption: Dive into Spanish cinema (and more) with this year’s ‘Película>Pelikula’ lineup

blocks.text: PELÍCULA>PELIKULA, by the way, isn’t limited to Spain. The lineup also includes Brazil’s Cyclone, Argentina’s Mensaje en una botella, Costa Rica’s Tengo sueños eléctricos, and Peru’s Vino la noche.
If you want to explore Spanish-language cinema from different countries, cultures, and perspectives, these are worth checking out.

blocks.caption: Dive into Spanish cinema (and more) with this year’s ‘Película>Pelikula’ lineup

blocks.text: Don’t skip “Encuentros en el cine: En corto”, the festival’s showcase of five short films from the Philippines, Chile, Spain, and Mexico.

The Filipino shorts in the roster include Agapito, a film following bowling alley pin setters that’s being campaigned for Oscars 2027 consideration, and Elenita, Elena, Elaine, a visually experimental short that was previously screened at this year’s Cinemalaya. The program also includes Chile’s Voz de trompeta, Spain’s Gilbert, and Mexico’s ¡Abre las piernas!
The shorts screen on October 11 at 5 pm, offering a mix of Filipino and international perspectives.

blocks.caption: Dive into Spanish cinema (and more) with this year’s ‘Película>Pelikula’ lineup

blocks.text: That works, too.
From family and friendship to identity, migration, history, adventure, and more, ‘Película>Pelikula’ has plenty of stories to discover. You don’t need to speak Spanish to enjoy Spanish cinema.
Check the full schedule on Instituto Cervantes de Manila’s Facebook page, and see where your chosen film takes you. – Rappler.com

This piece was written by Rappler volunteer Betina Andrea Santiago. Betina is a visual storyteller whose work centers on childhood nostalgia and pressing social realities. She enjoys exploring how visual media can drive empathy and is eager to use cinema to spark meaningful dialogue. A graduating Film major from the University of the Philippines Diliman, she aims to produce human-centered stories that give voice to everyday communities.

articles.title: Activists plan legal action against police ban on entering security zone near Perth weapons expo
articles.summary:
Under new WA laws anyone who defies an exclusion order could face a maximum $36,000 fine and three years in prison

  • Get our

blocks.text: Activists and a Greens MP have threatened legal action after the Western Australia police banned at least 12 people entering a designated security area where the Land Forces weapons expo will be held in Perth from 6 October.
The police used special powers given to them by the WA government last month to ban the activists from entering the area surrounding the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre.

Two of the activists, 18-year-old Will Shanahan and 22-year-old Matilda Lane-Rose said in a media conference held with the Greens MP Sophie McNeill on Friday they would take legal action if police and the police minister, Reece Whitby, did not revise the ban.
“We’ve sought legal advice, and we think that we have standing to pursue a judicial review into this decision,” said Lane-Rose, who works as a staffer for McNeill.

Rose told reporters the police called her on Thursday saying she had been placed on the exclusion list, despite having no plans to attend the protest against the expo, which is being organised by the WA Anti-War Collective.

The legislation used to ban her and 11 others, called the Land Forces (Special Powers) Bill 2026 was passed last month. It gives police expanded stop-and-search powers and the ability to ban people from entering a security zone that extends from the Elizabeth Quay bus port to the convention centre for 10 days.
Anyone who defies an exclusion order could face a maximum $36,000 fine and three years in prison.

Whitby said at the time the legislation was “about making sure WA Police have the powers they need to keep people safe and effectively manage Land Forces, while respecting the right to peacefully protest”.

The Land Forces International Land Defence Exposition event is held every two years and is Australia’s biggest weapons expo. The last event was held in 2024 in Melbourne, and attracted a large protest where police were accused of using excessive force.
Melbourne activists Violet Coco and Brad Homewood are among the 12 people issued an exclusion order by WA police.

The companies expected to exhibit at the expo are not listed on the Landforces website. Last month McNeill made public the list, which included an Australian subsidiary of Israel’s largest weapons company, Elbit Systems, and the state-owned company Rafael Advanced Defense Systems.

The two companies have been criticised by a former member of the UN commission of inquiry, Chris Sidoti, for being “key enablers of the Israel Defense Forces in its commission of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide against the Palestinian people in Gaza over the last two years”.
Shanahan, who recently moved to Newcastle from Perth, said he had not intended to attend the protest given he no longer lived in Western Australia, but now planned to do so, to defy the ban.
after newsletter promotion
“I cannot sit and watch my home state be captured by global militarisation and be turned into an all-out police state,” he said.
On Friday, McNeill accused the government of using the legislation to target peaceful climate activists.
“They said that these powers were for people who had the propensity to commit violence, people who are a threat to the community,” she said.
“Instead, what we’ve seen is peaceful activists targeted … who didn’t even have any plans to be here in Perth next week. It’s outrageous.”

Lane-Rose was fined $2,000 last year after pleading guilty with other Disrupt Burrup Hub activists to attempted trespass and criminal damage at the home of the then Woodside boss, Meg O’Neill, in 2023.
Whitby and the WA police were approached for comment.

articles.title: Verdict on Sara Duterte may be out December 16 — Senate court spokesman
articles.summary: Senate impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol says the prosecution's dropping of witnesses fast-tracked Vice President Duterte's impeachment trial

blocks.text: NOT ENEMY. Senate impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol urges House prosecutors to focus their energy on building up their case.
SENATE YOUTUBE SCREENSHOT
Senate impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol says the prosecution's dropping of witnesses fast-tracked Vice President Duterte's impeachment trial

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court may issue its verdict in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte as early as December 16, spokesperson Reginald Tongol said Friday, October 2.

In a virtual press briefing, Tongol said the trial remains “aggressively” ahead of schedule despite the suspension of proceedings, and that the court could finish the case before the Senate goes on its holiday recess.

The court cut short the hearing on Thursday, October 1, and suspended the proceedings slated for October 2, after granting the defense counsel’s request to defer the testimony of Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura over confidentiality issues.
The trial resumes on Monday, October 5, with Buenaventura taking the witness stand.

According to Tongol, the prosecution’s decision to drop some of its witnesses has expedited the proceedings, saving the court 27 trial days. He also said the House prosecution panel is expected to finish presenting its witnesses on Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth by next week.

If the prosecution formally drops the bribery charges against Duterte, it may proceed with its formal offer of exhibits. The defense will then be asked to comment on the prosecution’s formal offer before presenting its own witnesses.
The defense has been allocated 30 trial days for its presentation of witnesses. Tongol said that if the defense uses all 30 days, the senator-judges could issue their verdict by December 16.
“If the defense consumes all 30 days they requested, then the verdict may come by December 16,” Tongol said in a mix of English and Filipino.
Under the pre-trial order, the prosecution listed 57 witnesses to be presented in 62 trial days. The defense panel said it will present 45 witnesses in 30 trial days. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Trillanes claims Sara Duterte has undeclared millions in time deposits
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte did not declare millions in time deposit assets in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth from 2007 to 2010 when she was Davao City vice mayor, former senator…

blocks.text: Published October 2, 2026 4:12pm

Vice President Sara Duterte did not declare millions in time deposit assets in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth from 2007 to 2010 when she was Davao City vice mayor, former senator Antonio Trillanes IV said Friday.
Trillanes issued the claim a day after he asked the prosecution panel to drop him from the list of witnesses for the impeachment trial of Duterte.
The former lawmaker said that based on the research of his team, the Vice President had undeclared dollar and peso time deposits from 2007 until 2010.
He said the Vice President also did not declare a million dollars worth of life insurance in her 2010 SALN.
“Siguro naman, iyong senator-judges, hindi na mababaryahan rito (Maybe the senator-judges won’t see this as a pittance),” Trillanes said at a press conference.
“Iyan po ang mga milagro ni Sara Duterte (That is the miracle of Sara Duterte),” he added.

During the same press conference, Trillanes also said that Cale 88 Foods Corporation as well as Tapang at Malasakit Alliance for the Philippines, Inc., which are declared assets of Duterte in her joint SALN with husband Manases Carpio, also received P319 million and P150 million, respectively, from the Chinese government and firms.

He also reiterated the allegation he made before the House justice panel in April 2026 that a certain Sammy Uy, an alleged drug lord, transferred P181 million worth of money to the Duterte family, including the Vice President.
On Friday, Trillanes said that the Vice President knew Uy when she was 21 years old, because Uy sold land to her in 1999. The former senator presented a copy of a Deed of Sale between Uy and Duterte.
"When she was 21 years old, Uy sold two lots to her. It is a total of 900 square meters. Uy was their family friend," Trillanes said.

During the House justice panel hearing on the impeachment complaints against the Vice President, Anti-Money Laundering Council Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura said that at least 18 bank transactions linked to Duterte and her family members, as cited in the affidavit of Trillanes, match the AMLC records of covered and suspicious transaction reports.

Buenaventura told the House committee on justice that 18 of the randomly selected transactions cited in Trillanes’ affidavit and testimony correspond to entries in AMLC records, including three transactions allegedly involving Uy.
Asked for the source of his findings, Trillanes said that these are based on official documents from government agencies and are all verifiable.

“Lahat po ‘yan ay backed up by official documents. SEC, PSA, and AMLC documents posted on the Senate impeachment court website. Maliwanag po 'yan. Hindi tayo gumagawa ng mga kathang-isip na allegations,” he said.
SEC is the Securities and Exchange Commission, while PSA is the Philippine Statistics Authority. AMLC is the Anti-Money Laundering Council.

“Subok na 'yan. Our research team will eventually share this with the prosecution, and they would ask the same question to the impeachment trial witnesses, kung papayagan pa. Baka iyong pro-China senators, mag-protesta naman,” Trillanes added.
GMA News Online reached out to Duterte's legal counsel, Atty. Paolo Panelo, for comment and will publish it once available.

The prosecution is presenting evidence for Article 2 of the impeachment case against the Vice President, alleging unexplained wealth due to alleged failure to truthfully disclose assets in her SALN and failure to divest in businesses as required for the President and Vice President under a Constitutional provision. —AOL/RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: 400 French schools closed on Friday as protests escalate into ‘urban violence’ – Europe live
articles.summary:
Dozens of schools have been damaged and nearly 3,000 teenagers have been detained since the start of the tensions

Some 100 schools have been severely damaged during French high…

blocks.text: Morning opening: French protests continue to escalate with 400 schools closed on Friday

blocks.caption: Jakub Krupa

blocks.text: Jakub Krupa

Some 100 schools have been severely damaged during French high school protests that escalated this week into “urban violence,” with 40 headteachers injured, according to the latest figures from the French education ministry.

The pupils’ grievances range from overloaded timetables and overcrowded classes to insufficient teachers and unbearable temperatures during heatwaves earlier this year. Riot police have been deployed to confront the increasingly violent protests.
Nearly 3,000 lycée students – aged between 15 and 18 – have been detained since the start of the protests, including 1,949 on Thursday alone, the interior ministry said.

During a call with local prosecutors last night, the justice minister Gérald Darmanin urged them to pursue civil liability claims so that parents are made financially responsible for damage caused by their children.
Meanwhile, education minister Édouard Geffray asked parents for help, warning that “children are in danger on the streets.”

But there are no signs of tensions going down, with first incidents reported near the Jean-Rostand high school in Strasbourg and the Simone-Veil high school in Marseille. Some 400 schools remain closed today.

blocks.caption: A student walks in a cloud of tear gas smoke as part of a student blockading protest near the Couffignal secondary school, in Strasbourg. Photograph: Romeo Boetzle/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Damages from this week’s protests are likely to go into hundreds of millions euros, with the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region reporting 25 million in damages.
I will keep an eye on that for you, and bring you all the latest from Ukraine and elsewhere in Europe, too.
It’s Friday, 2 October 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
Good morning.
Key events

items: 20m agoMorning opening: French protests continue to escalate with 400 schools closed on Friday

blocks.text: The prefect of Bouches-du-Rhône in southern France told BFMTV that the situation on the ground was “incomparable” to the riots on Thursday, with “far fewer demonstrators” joining the protests today.
11 schools in the region are affected, while 55 switched to e-learning, Jacques Witkowski told the broadcaster.

articles.title: Hidden cameras show some stores unlocking speed limits on e-bikes, selling e-scooters that go up to 120 km/h
articles.summary: A new hidden camera investigation by Marketplace shows how some stores are selling e-scooters and e-bikes with top speeds much higher than provincial speed limits and with recommended rider ages…
articles.byline: Bobby Hristova, Madeline McNair, Asha Tomlinson

image.caption: Marketplace visited some of Canada's most well-known big box and specialty shops in the Greater Toronto Area with hidden cameras rolling to test how easy it is to find an e-bike or e-scooter that either had a maximum speed or age recommendation contravening Ontario laws. (CBC)

blocks.text: Whether it's children cruising down a suburban street, drivers delivering food downtown or a daredevil taking their need for speed to the highway, electric bikes and electric scooters are becoming more common across Canada.

A new hidden camera investigation by Marketplace shows how some stores are selling e-scooters and e-bikes with top speeds much higher than provincial speed limits and with recommended rider ages younger than provincial regulations allow.

Most provincial traffic laws limit e-bikes and e-scooters to 32 kilometres per hour or less. Age restrictions, meanwhile, vary across the country, ranging from 12 to 18. The territories and some provinces have no minimum age to ride.

That means it is mostly up to local police services to enforce these rules at a time when the number of injuries caused by these vehicles is climbing yearly, and public calls are growing for stronger, consistent rules nationwide and better enforcement.

Marketplace visited some of Canada's most well-known big box and specialty shops in the Greater Toronto Area — Amego, Emmo, EZbike, Best Buy, Canadian Tire and Costco — that sell popular brands. The undercover journalists tested how easy it is to find an e-bike or e-scooter that either had a maximum speed or age recommendation contravening Ontario limits.

In Ontario, e-scooter and e-bike riders must be at least 16. E-scooters cannot travel faster than 24 km/h on a flat surface, and e-bikes cannot travel faster than 32 km/h, according to provincial laws.
10 of 12 stores exceeded Ontario limits
Of the 12 stores journalists visited undercover, salespeople at six stores told us or showed us how to bypass built-in speed limits.
While most stores reminded us of Ontario rules, 10 stores sold e-bikes or e-scooters with maximum speeds beyond Ontario limits.
Stores are allowed to sell the e-bikes no matter how fast they go, but Michael Pasquali, founder of the Canadian Electric Bicycle Association (CEBA), says it's "heartbreaking."
"Shops that are selling products that are way beyond the legal limit, they're putting a lot of people in danger."
Seven stores also had e-scooters for sale with manufacturer-recommended rider ages under 16, though some medical experts say e-bikes and e-scooters are too unsafe for anyone under 16.

items: Watch the full Marketplace investigation on Friday, Oct. 2, on CBC-TV and YouTube.

blocks.text: "It's not just a toy; it's a motorized vehicle," said April Kam, an emergency physician at McMaster Children's Hospital in Hamilton.
"We're seeing kids who are presenting with brain bleeds, with abdominal injuries, solid organ injuries."

Recently released data from the Canadian Institute for Health Information shows 150 people ages 15 and under were hospitalized for falls involving an e-scooter in the 2025-2026 fiscal year across Canada, compared to 54 the year prior. That's an increase of roughly 178 per cent — and reflects a steady year-over-year increase for the last three years.

The number of head injuries related to e-scooters has also increased, from 50 in the 2022-2023 fiscal year to 157 in the 2025-2026 fiscal year. Fractures, dislocations and or muscle and tendon injuries have more than doubled in that same period, with 544 last fiscal year.
The Canadian Paediatric Surveillance Program released its own survey in August and found 10 children have died from using devices like e-scooters and e-bikes in 2025.
Meanwhile, sales for the electric rides have more than quadrupled in Canada since 2019, with roughly 372,000 e-bikes and 76,000 e-scooters sold so far this year, according to Statista.
Marketing to kids 'deceiving' parents, doctor says
The youngest age recommendation the Marketplace journalists found was at Canadian Tire — a Razor e-scooter that hits a maximum speed of 16 km/h and is recommended for children who are eight or older.

"That just boggles my mind. Kids at this age don't necessarily have the developmental ability to maneuver these motorized vehicles," said Kam, who is also president of the Canadian Paediatric Society's emergency medicine section.
"It's very concerning that there's this huge market for selling children these motorized vehicles, essentially, and deceiving the parents and family, marketing them as toys."
Doctor says kids 16 and under shouldn't ride e-bikes, e-scooters
Razor, the manufacturer of that particular e-scooter at Canadian Tire, said in a statement its device meets U.S. safety guidelines that say eight-year-olds can operate slow-moving motorized vehicles.
The company said its e-scooter is safe when properly used, isn't meant to be on public roads and that riders should follow local laws.

In statements to Marketplace, Best Buy, Canadian Tire and Emmo said customers should follow local laws. Best Buy said rules for e-bikes and e-scooters are evolving and that it tries to keep product information updated.
Costco didn't comment on Marketplace's findings.
E-bike stores can modify speed controls
At an EZbike location in Richmond Hill, a salesperson told undercover journalists it sells e-scooters that can reach 120 km/h — a speed that could get you a ticket on most highways.

At other stores, some e-bikes have their speed limited to 32 kilometres, adhering to Ontario's rules. But when asked if they modify vehicles, a salesperson at an Emmo location in Toronto said yes, they could modify a bike to go up to 150 km/h for off-road use.
"That's horrible," said Pasquali, of CEBA, who owns his own e-bike store in Hamilton.
Emmo and the company that operates the Emmo stores Marketplace visited said in a statement that a product's technical capabilities should not be confused with what's allowed on the roads.
But as an employee at an Emmo in Vaughan, Ont., described it: bypassing the speed limiter is "just like a toggle switch."
E-bike stores can modify speed control
Passing on that kind of advice is "extremely unethical," Pasquali said.

"If you're showing consumers how to push a button and make it faster or offering to modify it to go faster with the caveat that you keep it off road, well, that's technically right. But most consumers aren't doing that, right?"

A salesperson at an Amego store in North York, Ont., went a step further, unlocking the 32 km/h speed limit in front of undercover journalists and revving the motor, showing the e-bike exceeding the speed limit and saying it could hit a top speed of roughly 50 km/h.
Amego said in a statement it does not offer or perform modifications, and its salesperson likely exaggerated the top speed.
EZbike didn't comment on Marketplace's findings.
Mom wants change after son's devastating injury
Amy Richards, of St. John's, became one of those parents pleading for change after watching her son spend 102 days in the hospital after losing control of his e-scooter.
Jayden King, 14, was riding his e-scooter on a quiet street in May when he hit a speed bump and lost control.

King's mom says he was wearing a helmet at the time of the accident but suffered a traumatic brain injury. He spent 21 days in a coma and had to have part of his skull surgically removed due to brain swelling. Once he's healthier, King will have to undergo another surgery to get the rest of his skull put back in place, Richards said.
Mom wants change after son's devastating e-scooter injury
He learned to walk, talk and eat again but still lives with a long list of issues, including memory loss.
"I can't remember nothing in my whole life," King said. He says there's not a chance he'll ride an e-scooter again.

Newfoundland and Labrador has no rules governing e-bikes or e-scooters, but a spokesperson for Government Services said in a statement that it has consulted the public and is looking at changes to the Highway Traffic Act to include micro-mobility devices.
Richards said it should have happened a long time ago, and no one under 16 should be able to ride one.
"We need to protect our children. That should come first and foremost," she said.
Pasquali says the federal government needs to step in and stop the sale and importation of e-bikes and e-scooters that can be modified with the flick of a switch.
Safety is top priority, federal minister says

Canada's Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon told Marketplace in an interview in late September that he has heard stories of people being injured riding e-bikes and e-scooters, and he wants to talk to his provincial counterparts about how to respond.
Most of the legislation governing e-bikes and e-scooters is provincial, he said, and there is "impetus" for provinces and municipalities to act.
But, MacKinon also said the federal government needs "to absolutely consider what we will do in terms of regulating the safety of those devices."
"We'll always work with safety in mind. Safety is our principal priority."

articles.title: It's the biggest Alberta separatist account on the internet. It has links to a movement leader
articles.summary: The account Rise of Alberta is anonymous and drives four times as much engagement as the next most popular account.

image.caption: The most influential social media account on Alberta separatism is called Rise of Alberta, and it has ties to independence leader Keith Wilson. (CBC News Graphics)

blocks.text: One of the most influential voices on Alberta separatism is not a politician or even a clearly-identified person at all, but a combination social media account and merchandise line that is among the independence movement’s breakout stars.

The RiseOfAlberta account was created in the spring of 2025 and describes itself as “accelerating Alberta’s journey towards independence.” Since then it has amassed almost 100,000 X followers with a firehose of shareable clips and AI-generated memes about Alberta.

“They’ll depict, for example, eastern Canadians as very bureaucratic, government loving people, whereas Albertans are these Wild West people that hate government and love building,” says Chris Ross, a senior analyst at the Media Ecosystem Observatory, a research initiative that studies Canada’s online world and recently released a report into the dominance of separatist influencers.
“It’s a very idealistic, utopian perspective of what their idea of an Albertan is.”

items: Follow all of our Alberta referendum coverage

blocks.text: In between separatist talking points, the account dabbles in the conspiratorial side of the movement, posting images of Alberta workers standing up to “globohomo,” derogatory online slang for the 2SLGBTQ+ movement, echoes Donald Trump’s call to see “mass immigration” as an “existential threat to Western civilization" and refers to climate change as “fake and gay.”
Many points are punctuated by an ad for an Alberta-branded blanket or hat.

Distrustful of mainstream institutions, some in Alberta’s separatism movement have constructed their own online world populated by independence-minded influencers. Within that, Rise of Alberta is a behemoth, driving four times the engagement of the second-most popular account, according to the report. (The account is aware of this, based on a response to a curious American back in January: “I’m the biggest Alberta Independence account on X,” it wrote. “Happy to chat.”)

But as the account has grown its influence, the person behind the curtain has remained a mystery. The account has not responded to curious social media users, nor did it respond to direct messages sent by CBC News and Radio-Canada asking about the account’s identity.

It’s also not clear where the money from the premium camo hoodies and charcuterie boards is going, though the account has said that the proceeds help cover the costs of the “tools” used to make its graphics.
Now, CBC News has found that the account has links to another heavyweight figure in the separatist movement, Keith Wilson, a lawyer who leads the Alberta Transition Council.

According to an analysis by CBC News and Radio-Canada, the same email address was used to set up the Rise of Alberta website, the site where merchandise is sold, and the website for one of Wilson’s companies and the site for the Alberta Transition Council.

When asked by CBC News, Wilson said that he was pleased that the account was so successful, and that it had come up with some “incredible, interesting and funny ads.” But he was clear he was not the one behind the account: “Not everybody’s interested in being famous, right?” he said.
“I can tell you, it’s not me.”

In a followup call and email, Wilson acknowledged that he knows the person behind the account, explaining that it was run by the person who had set up his websites — “a website designer and webmaster” — which was why the same email had been used.
He “clearly” had a relationship with the person, he said, but he declined to provide more detail or to identify the person.
“The individual has chosen to engage in political commentary anonymously,” he wrote. “I respect that choice.”
Wilson stressed he had no say over the content Rise of Alberta posted and had "nothing to do with" the money the store was making.
He does provide some assistance to the person running the Rise of Alberta account, he said, including listing its merchandise on the “store” tab of his personal YouTube channel.
“I let him do that,” he said. “It doesn’t cost me anything and helps him.”

Returns of unwanted Rise of Alberta merchandise are also sent to the mailing address for his law firm, he said, though he added there weren’t many. (“Those blankets are amazing,” he said. “I have three.”)

While the person posting on the Rise of Alberta account remains unclear, they frequently share video clips of Wilson, and comment positively on his activities in the separatist movement. With the launch of Let Alberta Decide in June, the account posted that it was “incredibly encouraging” that Wilson was helping lead a “serious campaign.”

Wilson, who has publicly debated former premier Jason Kenney on the topic of independence, is also very active online, but strikes a different tone. He tweets clips of his own commentary and links to articles from the news sites dismissed by Rise of Alberta as “fake news.” The post pinned to the top of his page quotes the French Enlightenment philosopher Voltaire.

Rise of Alberta “constantly amplifies Keith Wilson’s posts, essentially acting as a campaign tool, but without any of the normal consequences,” says Ross, who was the lead author of the Media Ecosystem Observatory’s recent report on separatism influencers.

This is particularly notable because Rise of Alberta is “by far” the most influential account driving the conversation about separation, Ross said. The recent report found the account is single-handedly driving 11.8 per cent of all online engagement about the upcoming referendum, he said.
One in five of the images posted by the account is an ad for merchandise, according to an analysis by researchers from Common Ground at the University of Alberta.

The second most influential account, according to the report, is Keith’s personal X account, meaning the two accounts get almost 15 per cent of the online shares, likes and comments on separatism-related content.

In a normal election, party leaders would be scrutinized over their online campaign materials, Ross said. But because there are no elected politicians championing the separatist side, that vacuum has been filled by highly active, anonymous social media accounts, he said.

“The movement is structurally revolving around the Rise of Alberta account online, but no democratic form of scrutiny can interface with it,” he said. “It is bizarre, but the result of a modern campaign organized outside of party politics.”

(Wilson disagrees with this characterization, pointing out that he has more than 80,000 followers and many other big accounts interact with his posts. Besides which, he says, the separatism movement predates the Rise of Alberta account.)
‘Slopaganda’: University researchers study AI videos promoting Alberta separatism
Last November, a social media user pointed out the similarities between something Wilson and Rise of Alberta posted, and questioned whether they were the same person. Both accounts denied it.
“It’s not, but I am flattered,” Rise of Alberta posted with a cowboy emoji.
“I am too,” Wilson responded.

CBC News and Radio-Canada were able to link the Rise of Alberta website and Keith Wilson via the emails used to set up their respective websites by using DomainTools, a web analytics tool. An archived version of the Rise of Alberta website also listed the same mailing address as Wilson’s law firm in St. Albert, Alta.

While Rise of Alberta’s website was registered anonymously, meaning the identity of the owner is not publicly displayed, the company hosting it provides an anonymized email address to contact the website’s owner.

That same email address was first used a decade ago to register the website for Veritas Litigation Support, a company founded by Wilson. Starting last year, it has since been used for 16 other websites, most of which are related to Alberta independence.
It was also used for the websites for the Alberta Transition Council, an independence group led by Wilson, and Let Alberta Decide, a registered third-party advertiser co-chaired by Wilson.
The email has also been used to register a site called Rise of Saskatchewan, which is not active.

items: Experts warn betting on Alberta separatism could influence results

blocks.text: Wilson said the person behind Rise of Alberta sets up all of his websites, and he’s not sure why the sites all list the same email.

“I have been using the services of the person who runs that account for my websites for many years, and I don’t track all of the other stuff that they do,” he said. “I just know the stuff they do for me and they’re very good at it.”

The origin story on the Rise of Alberta website says the account began in the spring of 2025 because the person behind the account “had become convinced that Alberta would be better off as an independent country, and [they] wanted somewhere to say it.”

Things really took off after Prime Minister Mark Carney was elected last year, and soon posts were reaching millions of people, the site says. A few months later, followers started asking for merchandise and the store was born. (CBC News sent messages to the Rise of Alberta website and Facebook page, asking about the person running the account, and did not receive a response.)

Wilson says the person behind Rise of Alberta is “highly skilled” and “very creative.” Wilson also said he hadn’t seen the posts in which Rise of Alberta referred to climate change as “fake and gay” or referenced “globohomo,” and reiterated that he had nothing to do with what that account posted.
There’s a cost to being a public separatist in Alberta, Wilson says. There’s the risk to your career, to say nothing of the physical risk, he says. He gets hate mail and death threats, he adds.

“There’s a logical explanation as to why someone would want to remain anonymous, and I’m going to go as far as to suggest it’s almost admirable that the person’s not seeking personal fame, unlike every other social media influencer.”

articles.title: Marcos on school shootings: Everyone has a role to protect kids
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Friday said that protecting children amid the spate of school shootings is everyone's responsibility.

blocks.text: Published October 2, 2026 3:48pm
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Friday said that protecting children amid the spate of school shootings is everyone's responsibility.
Since June, there have been three high-profile school shootings that saw the deaths of students. Marcos spoke about the matter during a visit to Patul Elementary School in Santiago City, Isabela.

“Ngayon po ay nakakalungkot na mayroon tayong nakikita na mga pangyayari sa ilang eskuwelahan. Nangyari po ito, tiyak ako na nabalitaan na ninyo ang nangyari sa Tacloban, nangyari sa South Cotabato, at sa Zamboanga. Ito po ay kailangan po nating bantayan nang mabuti,” Marcos said.
(It is saddening that we are seeing these in several schools. This happened, I am sure you have heard about it, in Tacloban, it happened in South Cotabato, and in Zamboanga.)

“Kailangan po magkasama tayong lahat. Hindi po lamang ang pulis, hindi lamang ang mga teacher, hindi lamang po ang mga magulang, hindi lamang po ang pamahalaan. Kailangan po lahat tayo ay magkaisa at magsama-sama tayo. Bantayan po natin nang mabuti ang ating mga kabataan,” he added.
(We need to be united. Not just the police, not just the teachers, not just the parents, not just the government. We all need to be united, and we need to be together. Let us protect our children.)
Marcos said that the government is doing everything it could to keep kids safe.

During his visit to the elementary school, Marcos also witnessed the rollout of the Kaagapay Program in the Cagayan Valley, which aims to help enable parents to recognize signs of bullying, abuse, and online risks in their children.

Authorities have suspected that the school shooters were influenced by malicious online actors. Debates over regulating social media and online games have ignited, but many experts urged proper and healthy communication between parents and children as a preventive measure.
“Bantayan po natin nang mabuti ang ating mga bata, ang ating mga anak. Bantayan po natin na hindi sila nasasama sa mga ganyang klaseng kagagawan,” Marcos said.
(Let us take care of the kids, our children. Let us guard them so that they are not involved in these things.)

The Tacloban shooting saw the deaths of three children, while the Zamboanga school shooting saw two—including the shooter himself. The latest school shooting, which occurred in South Cotabato, also resulted in three deaths, again with the shooter included. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: I opened cockpit door of plane while being attacked, Indian pilot tells Modi
articles.summary: Capt Smit Machchhar, who was stabbed on the Israel-bound flight, has been hailed as a hero.

blocks.text: Indian pilot Smit Machchhar has said he opened the cockpit door of the Israel-bound Flydubai plane to allow passengers to come in and halt its rapid descent.

In a video call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Capt Machchhar said he was on the ground and still being attacked by his co-pilot when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to do something.
"I was lying on the floor injured but I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside," he said.
"Others came in and also played a role [in controlling the situation]. I was of course fighting for my own life but at the same time I knew I was not going to let others die," he added.
Machchhar was attacked by another pilot onboard a flight bound for Tel Aviv from Dubai, forcing the plane to divert to Saudi Arabia.
Modi told the captain that "his courage, patience and quick decision-making saved the lives of so many people" and the whole country was proud of him.
The captain, who has also been hailed as a "true hero" by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, was taken initially to a hospital in Tabuk, a city in north-western Saudi Arabia.
He was later airlifted to Abu Dhabi where he is reported to be in a stable condition.

The Indian embassy in the UAE on Thursday said Machchhar was "in good health and recovering well". Ambassador Deepak Mittal said he was "proud of Capt Smit for his bravery" and "very reassured" to meet him.

articles.title: TIMELINE: How TBS 'evolved' through the years
articles.summary: TIMELINE: How TBS 'evolved' through the years

blocks.text: Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla recently announced the government’s crackdown against members of True Brown Style (TBS) who were allegedly involved in illegal activities, including grooming minors into crimes.
According to him, TBS is entrenched in all local government units (LGUs) in Metro Manila as well as in 78 provinces.

Remulla said the group originated in California 35 years ago and reached the Philippines about 25 years ago as a small group before developing into what authorities now describe as a criminal syndicate.

But TBS Worldwide urged authorities to not generalize all members as criminals, pointing out that many of them are “professionals, workers, parents, business owners, and ordinary law-abiding citizens.” It added that some members have been engaging in charitable works.
According to TBS Worldwide, this is how its group evolved through the years:
1991 - True Blunt Systah emerges

True Blunt Systah (TBS) was formed in 1991 and became rooted in the local hip-hop and street culture of the time. The group developed a strong presence in urban communities and established its own identity and network of members.
1993 - Original Hiphop Posse Brotherhood is formed

The Original Hiphop Posse Brotherhood (OHPB) emerged in 1993 as another street group with links to the local hip-hop scene. Like TBS, OHPB developed its own membership, identity and reputation in different communities.
1994 - TBS and OHPB merge

In 1994, OG Hoodaz of Tandang Sora Hood introduced TBS leader Don Lucas to OHPB’s Joseph Ceñidoza AKA Joseph Saitan and Maynard AKA Dorobo. The meeting eventually led to an agreement between members of TBS and OHPB to join forces.
The collaboration resulted in the formation of True Brown Style 13.
1995 - TBS 13 leadership is formalized
Before Don Lucas moved to West Covina, Los Angeles, California, Saitan and Dorobo visited him to formalize the collaboration and leadership structure of the newly formed group.
Saitan was designated as president.
During this period, Saitan also decided to stop accepting women into the TBS, “believing that their presence caused conflict and strife among the members.”
1995 to 1996 - Internal differences
The merger and name change initially created misunderstandings among some longtime TBS members, particularly those in the North, including Manila and Tondo.
Some members had helped expand TBS in those areas but were initially not included in discussions about the collaboration.
Differences in membership and the greater presence of women in the Galleria area also contributed to misunderstandings between members.
By 1996, the members were eventually informed about the changes and accepted the new structure.
Late 1990s - TBS gains notoriety
True Brown Style 13 continued to expand its presence while also becoming associated with criminal activities, violence, and legal problems, according to the account of TBS Worldwide.
The group's activities resulted in confrontations and strained relationships with some communities.
Early 2000s - Members begin reconsidering their direction
By the early 2000s, some TBS key members began reflecting on the consequences of their involvement in crime and violence.
Increasing incarcerations, violent incidents, and personal losses prompted members to consider changing the group's direction.
2000s - True Brown Style 13 rebrands
The group eventually adopted the name True Brown Style Worldwide.
The rebranding was presented as a break from its previous criminal identity and a commitment to positive change, both in the Philippines and among members abroad.
TBS said its new direction focused on community service, empathy, personal development, and respect for the law.
2026 - Government crackdown

Philippine authorities are now gathering intelligence and hunting down TBS members who were allegedly involved in illegal activities following reports of minors getting involved in criminal activities and school shootings due to bad influences online. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Japan's first mayor to take maternity leave lands on TIME100 Next list
articles.summary: Shoko Kawata's maternity leave drew mixed reactions in Japan, a country struggling to lift birth rates.

blocks.text: Shoko Kawata, Japan's first mayor to take maternity leave, has been named one of the 100 most influential rising stars by TIME Magazine.
The recognition comes weeks after the 36-year-old gave birth to her first child on 15 September.
Earlier this year, Kawata, who is mayor of Yawata City in Kyoto prefecture, was plunged into a national debate about whether elected officials should take time off for childbirth.
Her decision to take maternity leave drew a mix of support and backlash across Japan, a country that is struggling to lift birth rates.

Some on social media said having a baby is tough and Kawata is doing her best. Japanese society has failed to design systems with pregnancy in mind, one claimed. Another said Kawata is setting a wonderful example by putting her family first and making it easier for other women to enter politics.

But critics argued that stepping away from public duties is "irresponsible", and that if Kawata wanted to get pregnant "she should have done so before taking office". One said top officials wanting to take extended leave "should resign".
Others insisted salaries should be cut during maternity leave.

In a sit-down interview with the BBC before giving birth, Kawata brushed off the criticisms, proudly declaring she enjoys her job and believes now is the time for her to have a child and start a family.

"If we were to criticise politicians taking maternity leave, it means we are effectively excluding all women in their 20s through 40s - women who are capable of becoming pregnant - from public office," she said.

While Japan provides maternity leave for city workers, there is currently no legal framework for local elected officials. So Kawata worked with her office to create a plan. She transferred her authority to her deputy mayor Shigeto Nose for 16 weeks, while working remotely when she could.

On 15 September, Mayor Kawata announced she gave birth to a baby girl. She posted a photo on X, external, thanking those who had supported her, and doubled down on her goal to advocate for social issues nationwide.
"As I face the countless challenges that lie ahead and learn what it truly means to be a parent, I want to reflect those experiences in real time into the policies I pursue," she wrote.
"I want to confront the many challenges facing parents and children today from that same perspective, as someone living through them myself, and think about how we can find a way forward together."
